fields.description: AMR-to-Text is a task that aims at generating fluent texts from Abstract Meaning Representation (AMR) graphs.
fields.label: AMR-to-Text

fields.description: Abstract Meaning Representation (AMR) is a semantic representation language that encodes meanings of sentences in a structured and interpretable form. It represents sentences as rooted, directed, acyclic graphs that capture core semantic information, such as who is doing what to whom, along with additional details like modality, tense, and polarity.
fields.label: Abstract Meaning Representation

fields.description: Abstractive Summarization involves generating a concise and coherent summary of a longer text by interpreting and rephrasing the content in a more abstract or human-like manner. Abstractive Summarization aims to produce concise, coherent, and informative summaries by generating new sentences or phrases that capture the essence of the source material. This approach allows for flexibility in summarizing content but can be challenging to ensure the generated summaries are both accurate and coherent.
fields.label: Abstractive Summarization

fields.description: Acoustic Modeling involves the process of modeling and analyzing the acoustic properties of spoken language, specifically the relationship between the acoustic signal (i.e., the audio waveform) and the phonemes or other linguistic content of speech.
fields.label: Acoustic Modeling

fields.description: Acoustic Signal Processing focuses on the analysis, manipulation, and enhancement of sound signals, particularly in the context of audio and speech applications. It involves various techniques and algorithms for processing audio and speech signals to extract meaningful information, improve their quality, or achieve specific objectives.
fields.label: Acoustic Signal Processing

fields.description: Active Learning is a machine learning approach where the model selects the data from which it learns. The model queries a user (an oracle who can provide the correct output) to label new data based on what it thinks will improve its learning the most. This approach is particularly useful when there is a lot of unlabeled data and labeling it all would be too time-consuming or expensive.
fields.label: Active Learning

fields.description: Adversarial attacks refer to the manipulation of input data with malicious intent to deceive NLP systems. This is typically done by introducing small, often imperceptible alterations to the original data, which can lead to significant changes in the system's output. The goal of these attacks is to exploit the vulnerabilities of the NLP models and cause them to make errors or produce incorrect results.
fields.label: Adversarial Attacks

fields.description: Adversarial Defenses refer to strategies or techniques used to protect NLP systems from adversarial attacks. These attacks typically involve inputting deceptive data designed to trick or manipulate the system's output. Adversarial defenses aim to make the system robust against such attacks, ensuring the integrity and reliability of the system's performance.
fields.label: Adversarial Defenses

fields.description: Adversarial Prompting refers to injecting prompts that can be standalone or prepended to begining prompts and induce specific behaviors into the generative process, such as generating images of a particular object or generating high perplexity text.
fields.label: Adversarial Prompting

fields.description: Adversarial Training is a technique used to improve the robustness and generalization of models. It involves training a model with malicious inputs (adversarial examples) created to mislead the model's learning process. These adversarial examples are typically generated by applying small but intentionally worst-case perturbations to instances from the training dataset, which makes the model more resilient and capable of handling unexpected or misleading input data.
fields.label: Adversarial Training

fields.description: Age Bias refers to the discrimination or prejudice based on a person's age. It can occur at any stage of life, but it is most commonly experienced by older adults.
fields.label: Age Bias

fields.description: All-words Word Sense Disambiguation (WSD) is a task that involves identifying the correct meaning or sense of every word in a given text, based on the context. This is crucial because many words in a language can have multiple meanings, and understanding the correct sense is important for accurate language understanding and processing.
fields.label: All-words Word Sense Disambiguation

fields.description: Alternative Lexicalization Discourse Relation Recognition refers to the process of identifying and understanding the relationship between different parts of a text, even when they are expressed in different words or phrases. This involves recognizing synonyms, paraphrases, and other forms of alternative lexicalization, which can greatly affect the meaning and interpretation of a text.
fields.label: Alternative Lexicalization Discourse Relation Recognition

fields.description: Analogical Reasoning refers to the ability of a model to understand and apply logical analogies. It involves identifying patterns and drawing parallels between certain concepts or entities. For example, in the analogy "man is to king as woman is to queen", the model should be able to understand the relationship between man and king, and apply the same relationship to woman and queen.
fields.label: Analogical Reasoning

fields.description: Analogy Detection refers to the task of identifying analogies in texts.
fields.label: Analogy Detection

fields.description: Anaphora Resolution refers to the task of determining what a pronoun, or a noun phrase refers to in a given context. It's about resolving references in the text, especially when pronouns like 'he', 'she', 'it' are used, the system should be able to identify to whom or what these pronouns are referring to. This is crucial for understanding the semantics and the complete meaning of a text.
fields.label: Anaphora Resolution

fields.description: Anonymization refers to the process of removing or replacing personally identifiable information (PII) from a dataset to protect the privacy of individuals. This can include names, addresses, phone numbers, email addresses, etc. The goal is to ensure that the data can be used for analysis or machine learning without compromising privacy.
fields.label: Anonymization

fields.description: Argument Extraction refers to the process of identifying and classifying the arguments or components of a sentence. This includes determining the subject, object, and other entities in a sentence, as well as their relationships or roles.
fields.label: Argument Extraction

fields.description: Argument Generation refers to the process of creating or generating arguments on a specific topic using AI algorithms. It involves the use of machine learning and language models to produce relevant, coherent, and persuasive arguments.
fields.label: Argument Generation

fields.description: Argument Mining is a subfield of Reasoning that concerned with automatically identifying and analyzing the structure of inference and reasoning expressed as arguments presented in a natural language text, such as a debate, an opinion article, or a legal case.
fields.label: Argument Mining

fields.description: Argument Pair Identification is aiming to identify whether two arguments are interactively related.
fields.label: Argument Pair Identification

fields.description: Aspect-based Sentiment Analysis (ABSA) is a subfield of Sentiment Analysis that is concerned with automatically identifying and analyzing the sentiment of a natural language text with respect to various aspects or facets rather than considering the text as a whole.
fields.label: Aspect-based Sentiment Analysis

fields.description: Aspect-specific Sentence Embeddings refer to the representation of sentences in a vector space that provide similarities between texts based on certain predefined aspects. The aspects are inherent properties of texts that must be considered when predicting their semantic similarity. Based on the different aspects focused on in texts, their similarities can be perceived very differently. Aspect-based Sentence Embeddings may represent a text not as a single generic embedding but as multiple specialized embeddings.
fields.label: Aspect-specific Sentence Embeddings

fields.description: Aspect Sentiment Quad Prediction (ASQP) analyzes the aspect terms, opinion terms, sentiment polarity, and aspect categories in a text.
fields.label: Aspect Sentiment Quad Prediction

fields.description: Aspect Sentiment Triplet Extraction (ASTE) is a task that aims to extract fine-grained opinion information from a given text. This information is typically in the form of triplets: aspect term, opinion term, and sentiment polarity. The aspect term refers to the subject or entity being discussed, the opinion term refers to the specific attribute of the aspect that is being commented on, and the sentiment polarity indicates whether the sentiment is positive, negative, or neutral.
fields.label: Aspect Sentiment Triplet Extraction

fields.description: Aspect Term Extraction (ATE) refers to the task of identifying specific aspects or attributes mentioned in text data. These aspects could be features of a product, service, or any other entity. For example, in a review about a smartphone, aspects could be "battery life", "screen size", "camera quality", etc. ATE is a crucial part of aspect-based sentiment analysis, where the goal is to understand sentiments expressed towards specific aspects.
fields.label: Aspect Term Extraction

fields.description: Attention is a mechanism that allows models to focus on specific parts of the input when generating the output. It helps the model to pay 'attention' to relevant words or phrases, and ignore the less relevant ones.
fields.label: Attention

fields.description: In an Attribute Inference Attack, an adversary has partial knowledge of some training records and access to a model trained on those records, and infers the unknown values of a sensitive feature of those records.
fields.label: Attribute Inference Attack

fields.description: Authorship Attribution refers to the task of identifying the author of a given text. It involves analyzing the linguistic style, word usage, syntax, and other textual features to determine the most likely author. This concept is widely used in fields like forensics, literature, and cybersecurity.
fields.label: Authorship Attribution

fields.description: Authorship Obfuscation refers to the process of concealing or altering the writing style of a text to hide the identity of the original author. This is typically done using various techniques such as changing the vocabulary, syntax, or structure of the text. The goal is to protect the author's privacy or to prevent authorship attribution techniques from accurately identifying the author.
fields.label: Authorship Obfuscation

fields.description: In Authorship Verification, texts of known authorship by one author are presented to a system, which is then tasked to verify whether another text has also been written by that same author
fields.label: Authorship Verification

fields.description: Autoencoder is a type of artificial neural network used for learning efficient codings of input data. It's designed to reconstruct its inputs, which forces the model to learn representations of the data in a compressed form.
fields.label: Autoencoder

fields.description: Automatic Essay Scoring (AES) is the use of specialized computer programs to assign grades to essays written in an educational setting. It is a method of educational assessment and an application of natural language processing. Its objective is to classify a large set of textual entities into a small number of discrete categories, corresponding to the possible grades.
fields.label: Automatic Essay Scoring

fields.description: Automatic Post-Editing (APE) refers to the process of automatically correcting errors in machine-translated text by learning from human corrections.
fields.label: Automatic Post-Editing

fields.description: Back Translation involves translating a sentence from the source language to the target language, and then translating it back to the source language.
fields.label: Back Translation

fields.description: Backdoor Attacks inject triggers into the specified models that make the backdoored model learn to predict badly on samples with triggers.
fields.label: Backdoor Attacks

fields.description: Backdoor Defenses are effective against Backdoor Attacks that inject triggers into the specified models that make the backdoored model learn to predict badly on samples with triggers.
fields.label: Backdoor Defenses

fields.description: Bag-of-Words (BoW) is a model where a text (such as a sentence or a document) is represented as the bag (multiset) of its words, disregarding grammar and even word order but keeping multiplicity.
fields.label: Bag-of-Words

fields.description: Biases & Fairness in NLP refer to the systematic and potentially harmful errors that arise as a result of a given choice of texts used to train a model.
fields.label: Biases & Fairness in NLP

fields.description: Bilingual Lexicon Induction (BLI) refers to the process of automatically generating a bilingual dictionary or lexicon. This involves mapping words in one language to their equivalents in another language, typically using machine learning algorithms.
fields.label: Bilingual Lexicon Induction

fields.description: Binary Classification is a type of classification that deals with only two classes or categories. It is used to predict which of two possible classes an instance of data belongs to. It's essentially a yes/no decision.
fields.label: Binary Classification

fields.description: Captioning is a subfield of Text Generation that deals with the automatic generation of textual descriptions or captions for visual data, such as images and videos. This involves understanding the content of the visual data and generating a coherent and informative description that accurately reflects the visual information.
fields.label: Captioning

fields.description: Chatbots are designed to simulate human conversation, typically through text or voice interactions. They aim to understand and respond to user queries, providing automated assistance, information, or services in a conversational manner.
fields.label: Chatbots

fields.description: Chunking is a subfield of Syntactic Text Processing that deals with the automatic identification and grouping of coherent sequences of words or other linguistic units that form grammatically meaningful units or phrases in a sentence.
fields.label: Chunking

fields.description: Claim Detection refers to the process of identifying claims or assertions from a given text that should be selected for verification.
fields.label: Claim Detection

fields.description: Claim Verification is the task of to assessing the veracity of a claim based on available evidence.
fields.label: Claim Verification

fields.description: Closed Book Question Answering is a task where a model answers questions based on the knowledge it has been trained on, without the ability to access or retrieve information from external sources or databases. The model relies solely on its internal knowledge learned during training.
fields.label: Closed Book Question Answering

fields.description: Closed Domain Question Answering refers to a type of question answering system where the system is expected to answer questions from a specific field or domain, such as medicine, law, or sports. The system is designed with a limited and fixed set of data, and it can only provide answers that are within this predefined data set.
fields.label: Closed Domain Question Answering

fields.description: Code Switching is a subfield of Multilinguality that deals with switching between two or more languages or language varieties in a single conversation or text.
fields.label: Code-Switching

fields.description: "Code-specific Language Models" refers to language models that are designed and fine-tuned specifically for tasks related to computer programming and software development. These models would aim to understand and generate code in various programming languages, assist with debugging, answer programming-related questions, and provide guidance on software development best practices.
fields.label: Code-specific Language Models

fields.description: Code Generation is a subfield of Text Generation that deals with the automatic generation of executable code, such as a computer program, from multimodal inputs such as incomplete code, programs in another programming language, natural language descriptions, or execution examples.
fields.label: Code Generation

fields.description: The goal of Code Search is to retrieve code fragments from a large programming code corpus that most closely match a developer’s intent, which is expressed in natural language.
fields.label: Code Search

fields.description: Code Summarization is a task that tries to comprehend code and automatically generate descriptions directly from the source code.
fields.label: Code Summarization

fields.description: Cognitive Modeling is a subfield of Linguistics & Cognitive Natural Language Processing that is concerned with modeling and simulating human cognitive processes in various forms, especially in a computational or mathematical form. This includes analyzing the cognitive processes and mechanisms underlying natural language use and developing models and simulations that can capture and predict human behavior and performance on language-related tasks.
fields.label: Cognitive Modeling

fields.description: Commonsense Question Answering refers to the ability of an AI system to answer questions that require understanding of everyday facts and general knowledge that are usually known to humans. It involves the application of commonsense reasoning, which is a key aspect of human intelligence, allowing the system to infer and predict answers even when not all information is explicitly stated in the text.
fields.label: Commonsense Question Answering

fields.description: Commonsense Reasoning is a subfield of Reasoning that is concerned with the development of algorithms and models for reasoning about everyday situations and concepts that are not explicitly stated in the text but require "common sense" or world knowledge and are commonly understood by humans. This world knowledge includes judgments about the nature of physical objects, taxonomic properties, or peoples' intentions.
fields.label: Commonsense Reasoning

fields.description: Compositional Semantic Parsing refers to the process of converting natural language into a structured, machine-understandable representation. It involves understanding the meaning of individual words, the grammatical structure of the sentence, and how these elements combine to produce the overall meaning. The "compositional" aspect refers to the idea that the meaning of a sentence is built up from the meanings of its parts and the way they are syntactically combined.
fields.label: Compositional Semantic Parsing

fields.description: Conditional Random Field (CRF) is a statistical modeling method often used for structured prediction. It's a type of discriminative undirected probabilistic graphical model that predicts a sequence of labels for a sequence of input samples. It's particularly used in tasks like named entity recognition, part of speech tagging, and text chunking where context is crucial to predict the output. Unlike other methods, CRF takes into account the context within the input sequence to make a prediction, which often results in improved accuracy.
fields.label: Conditional Random Field

fields.description: Confounding Bias refers to the distortion that occurs when the effect of multiple variables on a response is mixed up. This bias can lead to incorrect conclusions about the relationships between variables. For example, a model might incorrectly attribute an effect to one variable when it is actually caused by another variable that wasn't accounted for. This can be particularly problematic in NLP when trying to understand the influence of specific words or phrases on the outcome of a language model.
fields.label: Confounding Bias

fields.description: Constituency Parse Tree is a tree representation of the syntactic structure of a sentence according to constituency grammar rules. Each node of the tree represents a constituent (word or group of words) and the edges represent the grammatical relationship between them. The root of the tree represents the entire sentence.
fields.label: Constituency Parse Tree

fields.description: Constituency Parsing is the task of analyzing the grammatical structure of a sentence by dividing it into hierarchical, nested phrases or constituents. It aims to identify the syntactic relationships between words and group them into parts of speech, such as noun phrases and verb phrases, to create a parse tree that represents the sentence's grammatical structure.
fields.label: Constituency Parsing

fields.description: Constituency Trees are graphical representations that depict the organization and hierarchical structure of sentences. They are based on the syntax of the language and show how a sentence is divided into its constituent parts (like phrases or individual words), and how these parts are related to each other.
fields.label: Constituency Tree

fields.description: Construction Grammar (CxG) is a usage-based approach to language which views grammatical structure as a set of form-meaning mappings called a constructicon. From this usage-based perspective, a construction could belong in the grammar either (i) because it is sufficiently entrenched (i.e., frequent) that it is stored and processed as a unique item or (ii) because it is sufficiently irregular (i.e., idiomatic) that it requires a unique grammatical description (Goldberg, 2006). The advantage of CxG from this perspective is that it focuses on explaining the creativity, the flexibility, and the idiosyncrasy of actual language use in real-world settings
fields.label: Construction Grammar

fields.description: Contextualized Embeddings refer to the representation of words that capture their meanings based on the surrounding context. Unlike traditional embeddings that assign a fixed vector to each word regardless of its context, contextualized embeddings assign different vectors to the same word depending on its usage in a sentence. This allows the model to better understand nuances in language.
fields.label: Contextualized Embeddings

fields.description: Controllable Text Generation (CTG) is the task of generating natural sentences whose attributes can be controlled. The attributes to control can range from being stylistic such politeness, sentiment, formality, etc.; demographic attributes of the person writing the text such as gender, age, etc.; content such as information, keywords, entities, etc.; ordering of information, events, like plot summaries etc. It is regarded as crucial for the development of advanced text generation technologies that better meet the specific constraints in practical applications.
fields.label: Controllable Text Generation

fields.description: Conversational Machine Comprehension (CMC) expects the machine to understand an open-domain natural language text and thereafter engage in a multi-turn conversation to answer questions related to the text.
fields.label: Conversational Machine Comprehension

fields.description: Conversational Question Answering (CQA) is a natural language processing task that involves answering a series of questions within the context of an ongoing conversation or dialogue. It goes beyond traditional question-answering systems by considering the conversational history and previous responses to provide more contextually relevant and coherent answers. CQA systems aim to understand the nuances of a conversation and provide accurate responses that take into account the conversation's evolving context.
fields.label: Conversational Question Answering

fields.description: Coreference Resolution is a subfield of Information Extraction & Text Mining that deals with identifying all expressions that refer to the same entity in a text. In other words, it is the task of determining which pronouns, nouns, or phrases in a text refer to the same person, place, thing, or concept.
fields.label: Coreference Resolution

fields.description: Cross-Lingual Transfer is a subfield of Multilinguality that deals with developing techniques and models for transferring knowledge learned from one language to solve tasks in another, commonly more low-resource, language.
fields.label: Cross-Lingual Transfer

fields.description: Curriculum Learning (CL) is a training strategy where the model learns from easy examples first and gradually from more complex ones, similar to how humans learn. This approach is based on the idea that a model can perform better if it first learns to predict simpler patterns before attempting to understand more complex structures. It's like a learning schedule or syllabus for the model.
fields.label: Curriculum Learning

fields.description: Structured Data-to-Text is a task that involves converting structured data, often in the form of tables, databases, or other organized data formats, into human-readable and coherent natural language text. The goal of structured data-to-text systems is to automatically generate descriptive and informative narratives or textual summaries that convey the key information contained within the structured data.
fields.label: Structured Data-to-Text

fields.description: Data Augmentation is a strategy used to increase the amount and diversity of data. It involves creating new synthetic data by slightly altering the existing data, such as changing the word order, replacing words with their synonyms, or translating sentences to another language and then back to the original language. This technique helps improve the performance and robustness of NLP models by providing more varied training data.
fields.label: Data Augmentation

fields.description: De-Identification is the task of hiding personally identifiable information (PII) in a dataset to protect the privacy of individuals.
fields.label: De-Identification

fields.description: Debiasing refers to the process of reducing or eliminating biases that may exist in the data used for machine learning or AI models. Debiasing techniques aim to ensure that the AI models treat all inputs fairly and do not perpetuate harmful stereotypes or prejudices.
fields.label: Debiasing

fields.description: Decision Trees are machine learning models used for making predictions based on certain decision rules. They use a tree-like model of decisions where each internal node represents a "test" on an attribute, each branch represents the outcome of the test, and each leaf node represents a class label (decision taken after computing all attributes).
fields.label: Decision Tree

fields.description: Decoding refers to the methods used to translate the output of a language model (usually in the form of encoded tokens or probabilities) into a human-readable text. These strategies determine how the model selects the next word in a sequence, balancing between diversity and accuracy.
fields.label: Decoding

fields.description: Dense Document Retrieval refers to the process of retrieving relevant documents from a large corpus based on semantic similarity rather than keyword matching. It uses dense vector representations (embeddings) of documents and queries to calculate their similarity. This approach allows for a more nuanced understanding of the content, as it can capture semantic relationships between words and phrases, and can retrieve relevant documents even if they do not share exact keywords with the query.
fields.label: Dense Document Retrieval

fields.description: Dense Embeddings refer to the representation of words or phrases in a continuous vector space. Each word or phrase is mapped to a vector of real numbers, which capture the semantic meaning and context of the word. These vectors are called "dense" because they are usually high-dimensional and contain non-zero values, as opposed to sparse vectors which contain many zeros. Dense embeddings are used to reduce the dimensionality of text data and are a key part of many NLP tasks.
fields.label: Dense Embeddings

fields.description: Dense Passage Retrieval (DPR) is a method for retrieving relevant information from a large text corpus. Unlike traditional methods that rely on sparse lexical matches, DPR uses dense vector representations of text passages and queries to find relevant information. This approach allows for more nuanced understanding of the text, as it can capture semantic similarities beyond exact word matches.
fields.label: Dense Passage Retrieval

fields.description: Dependency Graphs represent the grammatical structure of a sentence based on dependency grammar. Each word in the sentence is a node in the graph and the edges between nodes represent the grammatical relationships between the words. These relationships help in understanding the context and meaning of the sentence.
fields.label: Dependency Graphs

fields.description: Dependency Parsing is a technique used to determine the grammatical structure of a sentence based on the dependencies between the words. It helps to understand the relationship between words, where one word is the dependent of another.
fields.label: Dependency Parsing

fields.description: Dialogue Discourse Parsing refers to the process of analyzing and structuring the conversational flow and structure within a dialogue or conversation. It involves identifying the the discourse links and corresponding relations between individual utterances or sentences in a multi-participant conversation to understand how they contribute to the overall meaning and coherence of the conversation.
fields.label: Dialogue Discourse Parsing

fields.description: Dialogue Management refers to the process of controlling and orchestrating a conversation between a computer system or chatbot and a user. It involves managing the flow of conversation, understanding user inputs, generating appropriate responses, and maintaining context throughout the interaction to ensure a coherent and effective dialogue. Dialogue management is a crucial component of building conversational AI systems and plays a key role in providing meaningful and responsive interactions.
fields.label: Dialogue Management

fields.description: A Dialogue Policy refers to a set of rules, algorithms, or models that govern how a conversational agent or chatbot should respond to user inputs in a dialogue or conversation. It defines the agent's behavior, including when to ask questions, provide information, or take specific actions based on the context of the conversation. Dialogue policies are crucial for designing effective and responsive conversational systems.
fields.label: Dialogue Policy

fields.description: Dialogue Policy Learning (DPL) refers to the process of training a machine learning model, often using reinforcement learning techniques, to determine the optimal actions or responses in a conversational dialogue. It involves teaching a system how to make decisions at each turn of a conversation to achieve specific goals or objectives, such as providing helpful responses or taking appropriate actions based on user input. Dialogue Policy Learning is a crucial component in building chatbots, virtual assistants, and other conversational AI systems.
fields.label: Dialogue Policy Learning

fields.description: Dialogue Response Generation is a subfield of Text Generation that deals with the automatic generation of natural language responses in a conversational setting, such as chatbots and virtual assistants. It requires understanding the natural language input and generating a coherent and appropriate response that follows the flow of the conversation, takes context into account, and adheres to social and cultural norms.
fields.label: Dialogue Response Generation

fields.description: Dialogue State Tracking (DST) refers to the process of monitoring and maintaining an understanding of the current state of a conversational dialogue. It involves tracking relevant information such as user intents, entity mentions, and context within a conversation. DST is crucial in building effective dialogue systems, chatbots, or virtual assistants as it helps in interpreting and responding to user queries accurately by keeping track of the evolving conversation context.
fields.label: Dialogue State Tracking

fields.description: Dialogue Systems & Conversational Agents is a subfield of Natural Language Interfaces that deals with the development of computer systems that can interact with humans in natural language. It involves the development of algorithms and models that can understand and generate natural language responses based on contextual cues, user preferences, and conversational goals.
fields.label: Dialogue Systems & Conversational Agents

fields.description: Dialogue Understanding involves the ability of systems to comprehend and interpret natural language conversations between humans or between humans and machines. It involves extracting meaning, context, intent, and relevant information from spoken or written dialogues to enable effective communication and decision-making.
fields.label: Dialogue Understanding

fields.description: Dictionary is a data structure that holds a set of words or phrases and their associated information. This information can include definitions, synonyms, antonyms, translations, and other linguistic attributes.
fields.label: Dictionary

fields.description: Differential Privacy is a concept that aims to provide a certain level of data privacy and security when processing and analyzing text data. It ensures that the results of any analysis (like machine learning algorithms) are essentially the same, irrespective of whether an individual's data is included in the dataset or not. This way, it prevents the disclosure of sensitive information about individuals in the dataset, providing a balance between data utility and privacy.
fields.label: Differential Privacy

fields.description: Discourse & Pragmatics is a subfield of Semantic Text Processing that deals with the analysis and understanding of language use in context, beyond the surface-level meaning of individual words or sentences. Discourse Analysis focuses on the organization and structure of text and conversation, and how they convey coherence, cohesion, and discourse relations, such as topic shifts, references, and implicatures. Pragmatics focuses on the study of language use in social and communicative situations, and how speakers and listeners use context, knowledge, and inference to convey meaning and achieve their communicative goals.
fields.label: Discourse & Pragmatics

fields.description: Discourse Analysis refers to the study and interpretation of written, spoken, or sign language use. It involves understanding, interpreting, and analyzing the broader context of communication, including the social, political, and cultural structures that influence text or speech. It goes beyond the understanding of individual words or sentences to comprehend how different parts of the text interact to produce meaning.
fields.label: Discourse Analysis

fields.description: Discourse Deixis Resolution (or Abstract Anaphora Resolution) refers to the process of determining the referents of certain types of expressions, such as pronouns or definite noun phrases, within a given discourse or conversation. These expressions often refer back to previously mentioned concepts or forward to upcoming concepts in the discourse. The resolution process involves understanding the context of the conversation and the relationships between different entities or concepts within it.
fields.label: Discourse Deixis Resolution

fields.description: Discourse Parsing (DP) is the process of analyzing and understanding the structure and relationships within a piece of text or conversation beyond individual sentences. It aims to identify how sentences and utterances are connected, such as through discourse markers, coreference resolution, and rhetorical structure, to extract a coherent representation of the overall discourse or conversation. This helps in understanding the flow of ideas, arguments, and information in a text or conversation.
fields.label: Discourse Parsing

fields.description: Discourse Relation Recognition refers to the task of identifying and categorizing the relationship between different sentences or clauses in a text. These relations can be causal, contrastive, temporal, etc.
fields.label: Discourse Relation Recognition

fields.description: Discourse segmentation refers to the task of dividing a continuous text or conversation into coherent and meaningful segments or units. These segments often represent distinct topics, ideas, or conversational turns within the text.
fields.label: Discourse Segmentation

fields.description: Discrimination Analysis refers to the study and evaluation of biases and discrimination that may be present texts or in language models. It involves identifying and addressing issues such as gender, racial, or cultural biases that can be inadvertently learned and propagated by AI systems. The goal is to ensure fairness, transparency, and accountability in NLP systems, and to prevent the perpetuation of harmful stereotypes or discriminatory practices.
fields.label: Discrimination Analysis

fields.description: Distant Supervision is a method used to create weakly labeled training data automatically. It involves using an existing knowledge base to generate labels for text data under the assumption that if two entities participate in a relationship in the knowledge base, then any sentence that contains those two entities might express that relationship. This approach is particularly useful when manual labeling of data is not feasible due to the large volume of data.
fields.label: Distant Supervision

fields.description: Distributional Semantics is a research area that develops and studies theories and methods for quantifying and categorizing semantic similarities between linguistic items based on their distributional properties in large samples of language data. The basic hypothesis is that words that occur in the same contexts tend to have similar meanings.
fields.label: Distributional Semantics

fields.description: Document Expansion is the task of expanding documents with terms that are related or representative of the documents' content to improve the retrieval effectiveness of a search engine.
fields.label: Document Expansion

fields.description: Document Retrieval is a subfield of Information Retrieval that deals with finding and retrieving relevant documents from a large corpus of textual data in response to a user query. It involves developing algorithms and models that can analyze the query and the corpus and rank the documents based on their relevance and similarity to the query.
fields.label: Document Retrieval

fields.description: Domain Adaptation refers to the process of modifying a model trained on one domain (source domain) to perform better on a different, but related domain (target domain). This is often necessary because the language use, terms, and context can vary greatly between different domains, causing a model trained on one domain to perform poorly on another. Domain adaptation techniques aim to overcome this issue and improve the model's performance on the target domain.
fields.label: Domain Adaptation

fields.description: Transformer Inference Optimization
fields.label: Efficient Transformers

fields.description: An Elementary Discourse Unit (EDU) refers to the smallest meaningful or syntactic unit in a discourse or text, often used for analyzing and structuring textual information. EDUs are typically used in discourse analysis to understand the hierarchical relationships and organization of sentences or phrases within a larger text, helping to break down and analyze complex language structures for various NLP tasks.
fields.label: Elementary Discourse Unit

fields.description: Elementary Discourse Unit (EDU) Segmentation is the process of dividing a continuous text or spoken discourse into its constituent units of meaning, often referred to as elementary discourse units (EDUs). These EDUs are typically short, coherent segments of text that represent individual ideas or thoughts within a larger discourse.
fields.label: Elementary Discourse Unit Segmentation

fields.description: Emotion-Cause Pair Extraction (ECPE) aims to extract the potential pairs of emotions and corresponding causes in a document. Typically it involves a 2-step approach to address the ECPE task, which first performs individual emotion extraction and cause extraction via multi-task learning, and then conduct emotion-cause pairing and filtering.
fields.label: Emotion-Cause Pair Extraction

fields.description: Emotion Analysis is a subfield of Sentiment Analysis that deals with the automatic detection and analysis of emotions in natural language texts, such as joy, anger, fear, and sadness.
fields.label: Emotion Analysis

fields.description: Emotion Cause Analysis refers to the process of identifying and understanding the causes or reasons behind certain emotional expressions in a given text. It involves determining what events, entities, or situations have triggered specific emotions.
fields.label: Emotion Cause Analysis

fields.description: Ensemble Models refer to the method of combining multiple machine learning models to improve the overall performance and accuracy in solving complex problems. This approach helps in reducing overfitting, improving the robustness of the model, and increasing the generalizability of the predictions.
fields.label: Ensemble Models

fields.description: Entity-Level Sentiment Analysis (ELSA) refers to the task of identifying the overall sentiment expressed towards volitional entities (persons and organizations) in a document.
fields.label: Entity-Level Sentiment Analysis

fields.description: Entity-based Coherence Discourse Relation Recognition refers to the process of identifying and understanding the relationships between different entities (like people, places, things) in a text. This involves analyzing the coherence or logical consistency of the discourse, which is the way these entities and their relationships are presented and developed throughout the text.
fields.label: Entity-based Coherence Discourse Relation Recognition

fields.description: Entity Alignment refers to the process of identifying and linking entities in different knowledge bases that refer to the same real-world object. This is crucial in integrating information from various sources and enhancing the comprehensiveness and accuracy of knowledge graphs. It involves matching entities based on their attributes, relations, and contextual information.
fields.label: Entity Alignment

fields.description: Entity Linking (or Named Entity Disambiguation) is a process that identifies specific entities in a text and links them to their corresponding entries in a knowledge base. This process helps in resolving ambiguities in text, as a single term can refer to multiple entities. For example, the term "Apple" could refer to the technology company or the fruit. Entity Linking helps in determining the correct entity based on the context of the text.
fields.label: Entity Linking

fields.description: Entity Resolution is the process of identifying and linking mentions of the same entity in texts or knowledge bases. It involves determining when two entities mentioned in texts or knowledge bases actually refer to the same thing, even if they are referred to in different ways. For example, "Barack Obama", "Obama", and "the former president" in texts and knowledge bases could all refer to the same person. Identifying and linking different representations of the same real-world entity (like a person, place, or thing) across various data sources helps in reducing data redundancy and improving the accuracy and reliability of a knowledge base.
fields.label: Entity Resolution

fields.description: Ethical NLP is a subfield of Responsible NLP that deals with the ethical and social implications of developing and using natural language processing technologies. It involves developing algorithms and models that can handle issues such as fairness, bias, privacy, and transparency, and designing systems that promote ethical and responsible use of the technology.
fields.label: Ethical NLP

fields.description: Euphemism Detection is a task to detect words or phrases that are used to softens an uncomfortable topic. Euphemism is a ubiquitous figurative language tool, wherein the speaker refers to taboo topics in indirect, metaphorical terms to convey politeness or formality. Identifying euphemism can reveal tacit facts about the speaker’s intention and the context of the utterance.
fields.label: Euphemism Detection

fields.description: Evaluation refers to the process of determining the performance or accuracy of a model or algorithm. It involves comparing the model's predictions or outputs against a set of pre-defined correct results (ground truth or gold labels). The choice of evaluation method usually depends on the specific task or problem at hand.
fields.label: Evaluation

fields.description: Event Argument Extraction is a task that involves identifying and classifying the roles of entities in events described in text.
fields.label: Event Argument Extraction

fields.description: Event Coreference Resolution refers to the task of determining when two expressions in a text refer to the same event. This is crucial for understanding the context and semantics of a text, as it helps in linking different parts of a text that are talking about the same event.
fields.label: Event Coreference Resolution

fields.description: Event Detection refers to the process of identifying and categorizing specific events or occurrences within a text. These instances can be anything from a simple action, such as a transaction, to a complex incident, like a natural disaster.
fields.label: Event Detection

fields.description: Event Discourse Deixis Resolution (EDDR) refers to the process of identifying and interpreting the meaning of event-related expressions within a given conversation or discourse. These expressions, also known as deictic expressions, are context-dependent and their understanding requires knowledge about the situation, time, or location in which they are used. EDDR involves resolving these expressions to provide accurate understanding and representation of the text.
fields.label: Event Discourse Deixis Resolution

fields.description: Event Extraction is a subfield of Information Extraction & Text Mining that deals with identifying, extracting, and classifying events, such as accidents, elections, and natural disasters, from natural language text.
fields.label: Event Extraction

fields.description: Event Sequencing refers to the process of identifying and understanding the order of events as they occur in a text. This involves determining the temporal relationships between different events. Event sequencing helps in understanding the storyline or narrative structure of a text.
fields.label: Event Sequencing

fields.description: Evidence Mining is the process of retrieving and extracting useful and relevant information or 'evidence' from unstructured text data. This can involve identifying patterns, relationships, facts, sentiments, and other insights from text documents, social media posts, reviews, etc. Commonly, the task is being modeled that given a hypothesis as a query triplet, find the textual evidence sentences in a corpus that support the input query.
fields.label: Evidence Mining

fields.description: Explainability, Interpretability & Transparency (XAI) in NLP is a subfield of Responsible NLP that deals with developing algorithms and models that can provide transparent and interpretable predictions, and explain the reasoning and decision-making processes behind them. It involves developing techniques that can generate human-readable explanations, highlight important features and patterns, and enable users to interact and refine the models.
fields.label: Explainability, Interpretability & Transparency in NLP

fields.description: Explicit Discourse Relation Recognition refers to the task of identifying and classifying the relationship between two or more sentences or clauses in a text based on explicit discourse connectives. These connectives are words or phrases like "because", "however", "in addition", which explicitly signal the type of discourse relation such as cause-effect, contrast, or addition. This recognition is crucial for understanding the overall coherence and meaning of a text.
fields.label: Explicit Discourse Relation Recognition

fields.description: Explicit Semantic Role Labeling (ESRL) is the task of assigning labels to words or phrases in a sentence that indicate their semantic role in the sentence. These roles can include the agent (doer of the action), the patient (receiver of the action), the instrument (means by which the action is performed), etc. The goal is to achieve a deeper understanding of the sentence by identifying how different components relate to each other.
fields.label: Explicit Semantic Role Labeling

fields.description: Exposure Bias refers to the discrepancy between the training and testing phases of a language model. During training, the model is exposed to the ground truth data at each step, but during testing, the model only sees its own predictions. This can lead to the accumulation of errors during testing, as the model has not been trained to correct its own mistakes. This discrepancy and its potential impact on the model's performance is known as Exposure Bias.
fields.label: Exposure Bias

fields.description: Extractive Question Answering is task where a model extracts a specific span of text or passage from a given document to answer a question. The model selects and outputs a segment of text directly from the source document that contains the answer to the question. Extractive QA systems are designed to identify and extract the most relevant information from a text corpus to provide accurate answers to user queries.
fields.label: Extractive Question Answering

fields.description: Extractive Summarization involves automatically selecting and extracting key sentences or phrases from a text document to create a concise summary. Extractive Summarization identifies and reuses the most informative and relevant content from the original text to produce a summary that captures the main ideas and important details.
fields.label: Extractive Summarization

fields.description: Automated Fact-Checking is a subfield of Reasoning that deals with the task of automatically verifying the veracity of facts or claims in natural language text, by comparing them against a knowledge base or external sources of information. It involves developing algorithms and models that can analyze the text and identify the relevant facts and evidence, and reason about the likelihood of the facts or claims being true or false.
fields.label: Automated Fact-Checking

fields.description: Fact Discourse Deixis Resolution (FDDR) refers to the process of identifying and interpreting factual information that is context-dependent within a discourse or conversation. Deixis are words or phrases that cannot be fully understood without additional contextual information. In the case of FDDR, the focus is on resolving the meaning of such expressions when they refer to factual information, which can be crucial for understanding the overall context and meaning of a text.
fields.label: Fact Discourse Deixis Resolution

fields.description: Factual Verification (FV) refers to the task of finding reliable documents to verify a given claim and generate a verdict about the veracity of the claim.
fields.label: Factual Verification

fields.description: Fake News Detection refers to the application of NLP techniques to identify and filter out false information or "fake news". This involves analyzing the text data, and understanding the context, sentiment, and other linguistic features to determine the authenticity of the information.
fields.label: Fake News Detection

fields.description: Federated Learning is a machine learning approach where a model is trained across multiple decentralized devices or servers holding local data samples, without exchanging them. This approach addresses privacy concerns and reduces the amount of data that needs to be sent over the network. The model learns from data located at the source, updates itself and shares only the model updates, keeping the raw data localized.
fields.label: Federated Learning

fields.description: Few-shot Learning (FSL) refers to the ability of a machine learning model to understand and start performing a task with a very small amount of training data, typically just a few examples. This concept is inspired by the human ability to acquire new knowledge with a small number of examples. In NLP, this could mean learning to understand and generate text in a new language or understanding the sentiment of a sentence with just a few training examples.
fields.label: Few-shot Learning

fields.description: Figurative Language refers to the use of words or expressions that deviate from their literal interpretation in order to achieve a particular effect or emphasis. This includes similes, personification, hyperbole, idioms, etc. Understanding and processing figurative language is a complex task in NLP as it requires contextual understanding and often cultural knowledge.
fields.label: Figurative Language

fields.description: Gazetteers refer to lists of names or entities such as names of people, places, organizations, or even specific industry terms. They are used in information extraction and entity recognition tasks to identify and categorize words or phrases in a text. For example, a gazetteer could be used to identify all city or country names in a document.
fields.label: Gazetteers

fields.description: Gender Bias refers to the unequal treatment or perceptions of individuals based on their gender.
fields.label: Gender Bias

fields.description: Generative Dialogue Response Generation refers to the process of generating natural and contextually relevant responses in a conversational setting. It involves the generation of text-based responses that mimic human conversation, making it appear as if a machine is engaging in a meaningful and coherent dialogue with a user.
fields.label: Generative Dialogue Response Generation

fields.description: Generative Question Answering is a task where a model generates human-like responses in natural language to answer questions posed by users. Instead of selecting a pre-existing answer from a set of options (as in multiple-choice questions), generative question answering models generate responses from scratch based on their understanding of the input question and available knowledge, making them capable of providing more contextually relevant and open-ended answers.
fields.label: Generative Question Answering

fields.description: In Goal Hijacking the new goal is to print a specific target string, which may contain malicious instructions. This process uses prompt injection to specifically bypass safety and moderation features placed on LLMs by their creators. Jailbreaking usually refers to Chatbots which have successfully been prompt injected and now are in a state where the user can ask any question they would like.
fields.label: Goal Hijacking

fields.description: Grammar Induction refers to the process of learning the grammar rules of a language from raw data. This involves identifying patterns and structures in sentences and using these to formulate rules that can be used to understand or generate new sentences.
fields.label: Grammar Induction

fields.description: Grammatical Error Correction (GEC) refers to the task of identifying and correcting grammatical mistakes in text.
fields.label: Grammatical Error Correction

fields.description: Graph-to-Text Generation aims to generate fluent texts from graph-based data.
fields.label: Graph-to-Text

fields.description: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) are a type of neural network designed to perform inference on data structured as graphs. They are particularly useful for tasks where data is represented as nodes and edges. GNNs work by passing messages between nodes in the graph, updating each node's state based on its own state, the states of its neighbors, and the features of the edges connecting them. This allows GNNs to capture complex patterns in the graph structure.
fields.label: Graph Neural Networks

fields.description: Graphs are used to represent and analyze linguistic and semantic data. They are mathematical structures that model the relationships between different entities. The nodes of the graph represent these entities, while the edges represent the relationships between them.
fields.label: Graphs

fields.description: Inference Optimization
fields.label: Green, Sustainable & Efficient Methods in NLP

fields.description: Hallucination Detection refers to the identification of instances where a language model generates text or information that is fluent and grammatically correct but factually incorrect or unrelated to the input. This phenomenon, known as "hallucination", can lead to the production of inaccurate or misleading outputs. The goal of hallucination detection is to ensure the reliability and accuracy of the generated text by identifying these hallucinations.
fields.label: Hallucination Detection

fields.description: Hallucination Prevention refers to the process of preventing or reducing the generation of incorrect or nonsensical outputs by language models. "Hallucination" in this context refers to instances where the model generates text that is fluent and grammatically correct but factually incorrect or unrelated to the input.
fields.label: Hallucination Prevention

fields.description: Hard Prompts or Discrete Prompts are text prompts with discrete inputs and made from interpretable words and tokens, usually hand-crafted by humans.
fields.label: Hard Prompts

fields.description: Hate Speech Detection refers to the application of machine learning and AI techniques to identify and filter out harmful content that promotes violence or discrimination against individuals or groups based on attributes such as race, religion, sexual orientation, or other characteristics.
fields.label: Hate Speech Detection

fields.description: Head-driven Phrase Structure Grammar (HPSG) is a framework in computational linguistics that uses type feature structures to represent syntactic, semantic, and morphological information about linguistic expressions. It is called "head-driven" because the head word of a phrase determines many of its syntactic properties. HPSG provides a formalism for creating detailed, machine-readable descriptions of natural language syntax.
fields.label: Head-driven Phrase Structure Grammar

fields.description: Hierarchical Clustering is a method which seeks to build a hierarchy of clusters.
fields.label: Hierarchical Clustering

fields.description: Hierarchical Phrase-based Machine Translation (HPBMT) combines the phrase-based and syntax-based approaches to translation. This approach that translates sentences by dividing them into a hierarchy of phrases, rather than translating word by word. This approach allows for more accurate translations by considering the context and grammatical structure of the sentence, rather than just the individual words. It uses a statistical model to determine the most likely translation of a given phrase within its specific context.
fields.label: Hierarchical Phrase-based Machine Translation

fields.description: Hybrid Machine Translation (HMT) is a method of machine translation that is characterized by the use of multiple machine translation approaches within a single machine translation system. The motivation for developing hybrid machine translation systems stems from the failure of any single technique to achieve a satisfactory level of accuracy.
fields.label: Hybrid Machine Translation

fields.description: Idiom Identification refers to the process of detecting and understanding idiomatic expressions within a text. Idioms are phrases that have a figurative meaning different from the literal interpretation of the individual words. This task is challenging in NLP due to the complexity and variability of idiomatic expressions in different languages.
fields.label: Idiom Identification

fields.description: Image-to-Text Retrieval refers to the process of finding and retrieving relevant texts based on a given imagery. It involves using techniques to understand semantic content of images and then searching for texts that best match or represent the content of the image.
fields.label: Image-to-Text Retrieval

fields.description: Image captioning involves generating descriptive textual descriptions or captions for images. The goal of image captioning is to create a meaningful and coherent sentence or phrase that describes the content and context of an image, allowing humans to understand the image's content without actually viewing it.
fields.label: Image Captioning

fields.description: Image Question Answering (ImageQA) involves answering questions about the content of an image using natural language responses. This task requires a system to understand both the visual information contained within an image and the textual information in a question, and then generate a relevant textual answer.
fields.label: Image Question Answering

fields.description: Implicit Discourse Relation Recognition (IDRR) refers to the task of identifying and classifying the hidden/latent or unstated relationships between different parts of a text. These relations are not explicitly stated through conjunctions or other markers but are inferred from the context and content of the sentences.
fields.label: Implicit Discourse Relation Recognition

fields.description: Implicit Semantic Role Labeling (ISRL) is the task of identifying and classifying the semantic roles of arguments in a sentence, even when they are not explicitly mentioned. It involves understanding the context and inferring the roles based on the given information.
fields.label: Implicit Semantic Role Labeling

fields.description: In-Context Learning (ICL) refers to the process where the model learns from the context provided in the prompt itself. It doesn't require explicit fine-tuning or training on a specific task. Instead, it uses the information given in the prompt to generate appropriate responses.
fields.label: In-Context Learning

fields.description: Indexing is a subfield of Information Retrieval that deals with creating and maintaining indexes of textual data. The index provides a way to quickly locate and retrieve relevant documents or passages that contain a particular term or keyword.
fields.label: Indexing

fields.description: Inductive Bias refers to the set of assumptions that a machine learning algorithm uses to predict outputs given inputs that it has not encountered before. It is the bias or set of preconceptions that a system has before learning begins, which guides the system towards a particular solution when faced with ambiguous or new situations.
fields.label: Inductive Bias

fields.description: Inference Attacks refer to the methods used to uncover sensitive information from seemingly non-sensitive data. These attacks use machine learning algorithms to infer or predict confidential data based on the patterns and correlations in the available data. For instance, even if a dataset is anonymized, an inference attack might still be able to predict sensitive attributes like gender, age, or health status based on the patterns in the text.
fields.label: Inference Attacks

fields.description: Information Extraction & Text Mining is a subfield of Natural Language Processing (NLP) that focuses on automatically extracting structured information and knowledge from unstructured textual data.
fields.label: Information Extraction & Text Mining

fields.description: Information Retrieval is a subfield of Natural Language Processing (NLP) that focuses on the automatic retrieval of relevant information from large collections of unstructured textual data. It involves developing techniques and algorithms to search, retrieve, and present information in response to user queries. Information Retrieval is concerned with understanding the meaning of the user's query and matching it with relevant information in the collection, taking into account factors such as word meaning, word similarity, and relevance.
fields.label: Information Retrieval

fields.description: Instruction Learning refers to the ability of a machine learning model to understand and follow natural language instructions given in the prompt. It involves training the model to understand and follow the instructions accurately to generate the desired output. This concept is crucial in developing intelligent systems that can interact with humans in a more intuitive and natural manner.
fields.label: Instruction Learning

fields.description: Instruction Tuning refers to the process of fine-tuning a pre-trained language model on a dataset of instructions. The goal is to make the model follow specific instructions in the input prompt. It's a way to control the behavior of the model without modifying the model architecture or retraining from scratch.
fields.label: Instruction Tuning

fields.description: Intent Recognition is a subfield of Sentiment Analysis that deals with the automatic identification and classification of the intentions or goals associated with natural language texts or utterances.
fields.label: Intent Recognition

fields.description: Irony Detection refers to the computational task of identifying ironic statements in text. This is a challenging task as it often requires understanding the context, the speaker's intent, and cultural nuances. It's a significant aspect of sentiment analysis, as misinterpreting irony can lead to an incorrect understanding of the sentiment expressed in the text.
fields.label: Irony Detection

fields.description: Justification Production refers to the process of generating explanations or justifications for a particular machine-generated verdict on a claim.
fields.label: Justification Production

fields.description: Keyword & Keyphrase Extraction is the task of identifying and extracting relevant words or phrases from a larger body of text. These keywords or keyphrases represent the core content or main topics in the text.
fields.label: Keyword & Keyphrase Extraction

fields.description: Knowledge Augmented Language Models refer to language models that are enhanced with external knowledge sources. These models are designed to improve the understanding and generation of text by incorporating information from databases, knowledge graphs, or other structured forms of knowledge. This augmentation helps the model to provide more accurate, detailed, and contextually relevant responses, overcoming the limitations of models trained solely on text data.
fields.label: Knowledge Augmented Language Models

fields.description: Knowledge Base Question Answering (KBQA) is a task that involves extracting information from structured knowledge bases or databases in response to natural language questions. It combines techniques from NLP and database querying to enable systems to understand and answer questions posed in human language by retrieving relevant information from a predefined knowledge base. KBQA systems aim to bridge the gap between unstructured text data and structured knowledge sources, making it easier for users to access specific information through natural language queries.
fields.label: Knowledge Base Question Answering

fields.description: Knowledge Bases refer to structured collections of information or data that are organized and stored in a way that makes it accessible and usable for computational analysis and reasoning. Knowledge bases typically consist of facts, entities, relationships, and attributes. These knowledge bases can be manually curated or automatically generated from large text corpora and are essential for enhancing the understanding and reasoning abilities of NLP systems.
fields.label: Knowledge Bases

fields.description: Knowledge Distillation (KD) is a technique where a smaller, simpler model (student) is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, more complex model (teacher). The aim is to transfer the knowledge from the teacher model to the student model. This is particularly useful in NLP tasks where deploying large models is computationally expensive. The student model, being smaller, is more efficient to use but still maintains a high level of performance by learning from the teacher model.
fields.label: Knowledge Distillation

fields.description: Knowledge Editing methods aim to precisely modify language models to incorporate specific knowledge, without negatively influencing other irrelevant knowledge. In knowledge editing, the update of a specific piece of knowledge in language models is typically formulated as an edit, such as rectifying the answer to “Who is the president of the USA?” from “Trump” to “Biden”. Regarding a specific edit, knowledge editing strategies typically modify the model output by either introducing an auxiliary network (or set of parameters) into the pre-trained model or updating the (partial) parameters to store the new knowledge.
fields.label: Knowledge Editing

fields.description: Knowledge Graph Construction & Completion refers to the process of creating and extending a structured graphical representation of information or knowledge. It involves extracting entities (like people, places, or things) and relationships (like actions or properties) from unstructured data, such as text, and organizing them into a graph format. Further, reasoning approaches can be applied to add missing edges or nodes. The knowledge graph can then be used to understand the context, semantics, and connections within the data.
fields.label: Knowledge Graph Construction & Completion

fields.description: Knowledge Graph Embeddings (KGE) refer to the process of transforming the entities and relationships in a knowledge graph into numerical vectors or embeddings. These embeddings capture the semantic information and the complex relationships between entities in a multi-dimensional space.
fields.label: Knowledge Graph Embeddings

fields.description: Knowledge Graph Error Detection refers to the process of identifying and correcting inaccuracies, inconsistencies, or discrepancies in the data represented in a knowledge graph. This could include incorrect or missing relationships, inaccurate entity attributes, or other forms of misinformation. The goal is to improve the quality and reliability of the information in the knowledge graph.
fields.label: Knowledge Graph Error Detection

fields.description: Knowledge Graph Question Answering (KGQA) refers to the task of using a knowledge graph, which is a structured representation of information, to answer natural language questions. KGQA systems extract relevant information from the knowledge graph to provide accurate answers to user queries.
fields.label: Knowledge Graph Question Answering

fields.description: Knowledge Graph Reasoning is a subfield of Reasoning that deals with inferring new knowledge from existing entities, relationships, and concepts in knowledge graphs.
fields.label: Knowledge Graph Reasoning

fields.description: Knowledge Graphs are graphs of data intended to accumulate and convey knowledge of the real world, whose nodes represent entities of interest and whose edges represent relations between these entities
fields.label: Knowledge Graphs

fields.description: Knowledge Representation is a subfield of Semantic Text Processing that deals with the representation, organization, and management of knowledge and information in a form that can be processed and used by computers in conjunction with natural language texts. It involves developing formal languages and frameworks, such as ontologies, semantic networks, and knowledge graphs, that can capture and represent the semantics, structure, and relations of concepts and entities in a domain-specific or general knowledge base.
fields.label: Knowledge Representation

fields.description: Language Grounding is the ability to tie verbal expressions to their referents in the non-linguistic world. The non-linguistic world can be physical or non-physical such as real-world objects, visual content, actions, or concepts. It involves bridging the gap between linguistic symbols and the underlying meaning or context.
fields.label: Language Grounding

fields.description: Language Identification refers to the task of automatically determining the natural language of a given content.
fields.label: Language Identification

fields.description: Language Model Adapters are a method of fine-tuning pre-trained language models. Instead of fine-tuning all parameters of the model, only a small set of parameters in added adapter modules are trained. This approach allows for a more efficient adaptation of the model to a specific task, while preserving the original model weights. It also enables multi-task learning and transfer learning, as different adapters can be plugged into the model for different tasks.
fields.label: Language Model Adapters

fields.description: Language Model Alignment is the process of ensuring that a language model's outputs align with the preferences and intentions of a human user. It involves training the model to understand and respond accurately to the inputs it receives, minimizing misunderstanding or misinterpretation. This concept is crucial in developing AI systems that can effectively and safely interact with humans meaningfully.
fields.label: Language Model Alignment

fields.description: Language Model Hallucination refers to the phenomenon where the model generates text or information that is fluent and grammatically correct but factually incorrect or unrelated to the input. It's a significant challenge in developing reliable and accurate language models.
fields.label: Language Model Hallucination

fields.description: Language Model Mechanisms refer to the design decisions and concepts used to build language models.
fields.label: Language Model Mechanisms

fields.description: Language Model Quantization refers to the process of reducing the precision of the numerical values in a language model to make it smaller and faster. This involves converting the continuous values into discrete counterparts. The main goal of quantization is to reduce the computational and storage requirements of the model, which can be particularly beneficial for deploying NLP models on devices with limited resources. However, it's a challenge to perform quantization without significantly impacting the model's performance.
fields.label: Language Model Quantization

fields.description: Language Models & Neural Networks is a subfield of Semantic Text Processing that deals with the probabilistic modeling and generation of natural language, based on a learned probability function of sequences of words. Language models generate probabilities by training on corpora of natural language texts and can be fine-tuned for a variety of different downstream tasks. Neural networks are methods in artificial intelligence (AI) that teach computers to process data in a way that is inspired by the human brain.
fields.label: Language Models & Neural Networks

fields.description: Learn to Knowledge Distillation is a concept that involves training a smaller model (student) to mimic the behavior of a larger, more complex model (teacher). The goal is to transfer the knowledge from the larger model to the smaller one, thereby improving the efficiency and performance of the smaller model. In the context of Meta-Learning, this involves to train a meta teacher model that works better than a single teacher model and to optimize the transferring process and force the teacher model to be aware of the student model.
fields.label: Learn to Knowledge Distillation

fields.description: Learn to Lifelong Learning refers to the ability of a model to continuously learn and adapt from new data or experiences over time. This concept emphasizes the development of learning algorithms that can not only learn from a single task but also generalize their learning to new tasks. It involves the model's ability to remember previous knowledge, adapt to new tasks with few examples, and not forget the old tasks while learning new ones (avoiding catastrophic forgetting).
fields.label: Learn to Lifelong Learning

fields.description: Learning to Compare refers to a method where the model learns to compare new information with existing knowledge. This is done by training the model on a variety of tasks, and then using this learned knowledge to make comparisons and predictions on new, unseen tasks. In NLP, this could involve comparing the semantic similarity of sentences or documents, or comparing the relevance of a document to a query. The goal is to enable the model to generalize from its learned knowledge to new tasks, improving its performance and adaptability.
fields.label: Learning to Compare

fields.description: Learning to Initialize refers to the process where the model learns the optimal initialization of parameters. This is done so that a few steps of gradient descent during the fine-tuning phase can adapt the model to a specific task. This concept is particularly useful in meta-learning where the goal is to design models that can learn new skills or adapt to new environments rapidly with a few training examples. In the context of NLP, this could mean adapting to new languages or new language tasks.
fields.label: Learning to Initialize

fields.description: Lemmatization is the process of reducing words to their base or root form, known as a lemma. Unlike stemming, which simply removes certain end characters from words, lemmatization considers the context and part of speech of a word in order to accurately convert it to its base form. For example, the word "better" would be lemmatized to "good".
fields.label: Lemmatization

fields.description: Lexical Sample Word Sense Disambiguation (WSD) is a task where the system is given a particular word along with a context, and it has to correctly identify the sense or meaning of the word in that context. This task is performed on a small sample of specific words, hence the term 'lexical sample'. The challenge lies in the fact that many words in a language have multiple meanings and the system has to accurately determine which meaning is applicable in the given context.
fields.label: Lexical Sample Word Sense Disambiguation

fields.description: Lexical Simplification is a task that involves replacing complex words in a text with simpler, more commonly used words, without changing the overall meaning of the text. This technique is often used to make text more understandable for a wider audience, including children, non-native speakers, or individuals with reading difficulties.
fields.label: Lexical Simplification
