fields.description: Lexical Substitution refers to the process of replacing a word in a sentence with another word that maintains the same overall meaning of the sentence.
fields.label: Lexical Substitution

fields.description: Linguistic Theories is a subfield of Linguistics & Cognitive Natural Language Processing that explores the nature of language and attempts to answer fundamental questions about what language is or what is the common basis of all languages. Additionally, the goal is also to provide a general theoretical framework that describes, explains, and predicts how language is used and processed.
fields.label: Linguistic Theories

fields.description: Linguistics & Cognitive Natural Language Processing is a subfield of Natural Language Processing (NLP) that focuses on the study of natural language from a linguistic and cognitive perspective. It studies natural language based on the assumptions that our linguistic abilities are firmly rooted in our cognitive abilities, that meaning is essentially conceptualization, and that grammar is shaped by usage.
fields.label: Linguistics & Cognitive NLP

fields.description: Link Prediction is the task of inferring missing links between entities in existing knowledge bases often performed via ranking entities as possible answers to queries.
fields.label: Link Prediction

fields.description: Long-Range Transformers refer to a type of transformer model that is designed to handle long sequences of data more efficiently. Traditional transformer models struggle with long sequences due to their quadratic complexity with respect to the sequence length. Long-Range Transformers address this issue by using methods such as sparse attention mechanisms or other techniques to reduce the computational complexity, enabling the model to process longer sequences of text while maintaining high performance.
fields.label: Long-Range Transformers

fields.description: Low-Resource NLP is a subfield of Responsible NLP which is concerned with the development of algorithms and models that work in resource-constrained environments, such as data scarcity and low-resource languages.
fields.label: Low-Resource NLP

fields.description: Machine Generated Text Detection refers to the process of identifying and distinguishing text that has been generated by an artificial intelligence or machine learning model, as opposed to text that has been written by a human.
fields.label: Machine Generated Text Detection

fields.description: Machine Reading Comprehension is a subfield of Reasoning that deals with the task of automatically reading and understanding a piece of text and answering questions about it, as a human would. It involves developing algorithms and models that can handle the complexity and ambiguity of natural language, and reason about the implicit and explicit information in the text to infer the correct answer.
fields.label: Machine Reading Comprehension

fields.description: Machine Translation is a subfield of Multilinguality and Text Generation that deals with developing algorithms and models for automatically translating text or speech from one language to another. It involves analyzing the input text or speech, generating a representation of its meaning in the source language, and then producing a new text or speech in the target language that conveys the same meaning.
fields.label: Machine Translation

fields.description: Math Word Problem Solving refers to the ability of an AI system to understand and solve mathematical problems presented in natural language. This involves the system's ability to accurately interpret the problem, identify the mathematical operations required, and perform those operations to produce a correct answer. This is a complex task as it requires a deep understanding of language semantics, the ability to handle ambiguity, and proficiency in mathematical reasoning.
fields.label: Math Word Problem Solving

fields.description: Media Bias refers to the perceived or actual bias of journalists and news producers within the mass media, in the selection of events and stories that are reported, and how they are covered. This bias can be in terms of political, economic, racial, cultural, or ideological perspectives. It can manifest in the framing of narratives, omission of certain facts or events, and disproportionate coverage of certain topics.
fields.label: Media Bias

fields.description: Membership Inference Attacks (MIAs) aim to predict whether a data sample was present in the training data of a machine learning model or not, and are widely used for assessing the privacy risks of language models.
fields.label: Membership Inference Attack

fields.description: Meme Classification refers to the task of classifying internet memes. Memes are graphics and text overlapped so that together they present concepts that become dubious if one of them is absent. It is spread mostly on social media platforms, in the form of jokes, sarcasm, motivating, etc.
fields.label: Meme Classification

fields.description: Meta-Learning in machine learning refers to the concept where the algorithm learns from the output of other machine learning algorithms. It typically refers to ensemble learning algorithms like stacking that learn how to combine the predictions from ensemble members. Meta-learning also refers to algorithms that learn how to learn across a suite of related prediction tasks, referred to as multi-task learning. It's essentially "learning how to learn". Meta-learning allows faster fine-tuning, converges to better performance, yields more generalizable models, and it achieves great results in few-shot settings.
fields.label: Meta-Learning

fields.description: Meta-Learning for Data Selection can be used to determine which data samples are most useful for training a model. This can be particularly when the amount of available data can be vast and varied. The goal is to optimize the learning process by selecting the most relevant and useful data for the task at hand.
fields.label: Meta-Learning for Data Selection

fields.description: Metaphor Detection refers to the ability of a machine learning model or algorithm to identify and understand metaphors in a given text. Metaphors are figures of speech that describe an object or action in a way that isn't literally true, but helps explain an idea or make a comparison. Detecting and interpreting them correctly is a complex task as it requires a deep understanding of the context and the nuances of the language.
fields.label: Metaphor Detection

fields.description: Misinformation Detection refers to the application of NLP techniques to identify and filter out false or misleading information. This can involve analyzing text data to determine its truthfulness, reliability, and relevance. It's particularly important in areas like social media, news, and online content where misinformation can spread quickly.
fields.label: Misinformation Detection

fields.description: Mixture of Experts (MoE) is a machine learning technique that involves training multiple models, each specializing in a different aspect of the data (the "experts"), and then combining their outputs. The idea is to leverage the strengths of each expert on the parts of the data where they perform best. This approach can improve overall performance and accuracy in complex NLP tasks.
fields.label: Mixture of Experts

fields.description: Model-Agnostic Meta-Learning (MAML) is a learning framework that aims to train a model on a variety of learning tasks, enabling it to quickly adapt to new tasks using a small number of training samples. MAML is "model-agnostic" in that it is compatible with any model trained with gradient descent and applicable to a variety of different learning tasks, including classification, regression, and reinforcement learning.
fields.label: Model-Agnostic Meta-Learning

fields.description: Model Inversion Attacks refer to a type of cyber attack where an attacker tries to extract sensitive information from a machine learning model. The attacker uses the outputs of the model and possibly some additional information to reconstruct the original input data or some properties of it. This can lead to privacy breaches, especially when the model has been trained on sensitive data like personal emails or confidential documents.
fields.label: Model Inversion Attack

fields.description: Model Stealing Attack refers to a type of cyber attack where an attacker aims to duplicate the functionality of a machine learning model without having access to the original model's parameters or training data. The attacker typically uses a series of queries to the model and uses the responses to train a replica. This can lead to intellectual property theft and potential misuse of the model.
fields.label: Model Stealing Attack

fields.description: Morphemes refer to the smallest meaningful units of a language. They are the building blocks of words, which can't be further divided without losing or changing their meaning. For example, the word "unhappiness" contains three morphemes: "un-", "happy", and "-ness".
fields.label: Morphemes

fields.description: Morphological Inflection refers to the process of using rules and algorithms to generate different forms of a word. This concept is based on the linguistic phenomenon where the form of a word changes to express different grammatical categories such as tense, case, voice, aspect, person, number, gender, and mood. For example, the verb 'run' can be inflected to 'runs', 'running', or 'ran' to indicate different tenses.
fields.label: Morphological Inflection

fields.description: Morphological Segmentation refers to the process of dividing words into individual units called morphemes. Morphemes are the smallest meaningful units in a language, which include root words, prefixes, and suffixes.
fields.label: Morphological Segmentation

fields.description: Morphology is a subfield of Syntactic Text Processing that deals with studying the structure and formation of word as well as their relationship to other words in the same language. It analyzes the structure of words and parts of words such as stems, root words, prefixes, and suffixes. Morphology also looks at parts of speech, intonation and stress, and the ways context can change a word's pronunciation and meaning.
fields.label: Morphology

fields.description: Multi-Agent Systems & Multi-Model Language Models refer to the combination of multiple agents or language models to solve problems that are difficult or impossible for an individual agent or a monolithic system to solve. Also, using multiple agents or models can improve the performance of natural language processing tasks.
fields.label: Multi-Agent Systems & Multi-Model Language Models

fields.description: Multi-Hop Reasoning is a concept where the system uses a knowledge graph or multiple text passages to answer complex queries by making multiple inferential leaps (hops). It involves traversing through the graph or text passages and making connections between different evidences to derive new information or answer a query.
fields.label: Multi-Hop Reasoning

fields.description: Multi-class Classification is a type of machine learning algorithm that categorizes instances into one of three or more classes. It is an extension of binary classification, which only categorizes instances into one of two classes. The goal of multi-class classification is to assign an instance to one of several different classes.
fields.label: Multi-class Classification

fields.description: Multi-label classification is a type of machine learning problem where an instance/sample can be classified into multiple classes or labels. In other words, it is not limited to assigning a single label to each instance, but allows for one or more labels to be assigned. This is different from multi-class classification, where each instance is assigned only one label from multiple classes.
fields.label: Multi-label Classification

fields.description: Multi-task Learning (MTL) is a learning paradigm where multiple learning tasks are solved at the same time, while exploiting commonalities and differences across tasks. This approach aims to improve the performance of individual tasks by leveraging the shared information among them. It's particularly useful in NLP where datasets can be scarce or imbalanced, as it allows models to learn representations across different tasks, enhancing generalization and robustness.
fields.label: Multi-task Learning

fields.description: Multilingual Language Models are models that are designed to understand, interpret, generate, or translate multiple languages. These models are trained on text data from several languages, enabling them to perform tasks across different languages.
fields.label: Multilingual Language Models

fields.description: Multilinguality is a subfield of Natural Language Processing (NLP) that refers to the ability of machines to understand, process, and generate natural language text in multiple languages. Multilinguality is concerned with addressing the challenges that arise due to the linguistic and structural variations that exist across different languages. This includes variations in word order, syntax, grammar, or vocabulary.
fields.label: Multilinguality

fields.description: Multimodal Language Models are advanced AI models that can understand and generate information from different types of data such as text, images, and sound simultaneously. These models are designed to capture the complex relationships between different data modes, enabling more comprehensive understanding and generation of content.
fields.label: Multimodal Language Models

fields.description: Multimodality is a subfield of Natural Language Processing (NLP) that refers to the capability of a system or method to process input of different types or “modalities”, such as natural language text, speech, audio, images, video, and programming languages in NLP applications. It involves developing algorithms and models that can process and analyze information from multiple modalities, and integrate them to form a unified representation of the input.
fields.label: Multimodality

fields.description: Multiword Expression (MWE) Identification refers to the process of detecting and classifying sequences of words that have a different meaning collectively than the individual meanings of the words. These expressions include idioms, compound nouns, phrasal verbs, etc. MWE identification is crucial in NLP tasks as it helps in understanding the semantic meaning of texts more accurately.
fields.label: Multiword Expression Identification

fields.description: Multiword Expression Processing focuses on the identification, interpretation, and utilization of multiword expressions (MWEs). MWEs are phrases or combinations of words that have a specific, unique meaning when used together, which cannot be deduced from the meanings of the individual words. Examples include idioms like "kick the bucket", compound nouns like "hot dog", or verb-particle constructions like "look up".
fields.label: Multiword Expression Processing

fields.description: Music in NLP refers to the textual or symbolic representation of musical information, such as lyrics, musical notes, scores, or metadata related to music. NLP techniques can be applied to analyze, generate, and derive insights from this textual data related to music.
fields.label: Music in NLP

fields.description: Named Entity Recognition (NER) is a subfield of Information Extraction & Text Mining that deals with identifying, extracting, and classifying named entities, such as people, organizations, and locations, in unstructured natural language texts.
fields.label: Named Entity Recognition

fields.description: Natural Language Interfaces is a subfield of Natural Language Processing (NLP) that deals with the development of interfaces that enable humans to interact with computers using natural language. It involves developing algorithms and models that can understand and interpret human language and generate appropriate responses.
fields.label: Natural Language Interfaces

fields.description: Natural Language Processing (NLP) is an interdisciplinary subfield of linguistics, computer science, and artificial intelligence concerned with the interactions between computers and human language, in particular how to program computers to process and analyze large amounts of natural language data. The goal is a computer capable of 'understanding' the contents of documents, including the contextual nuances of the language within them. The technology can then accurately extract information and insights contained in the documents as well as categorize and organize the documents themselves.
fields.label: Natural Language Processing

fields.description: Neural Machine Translation (NMT) is a method of automatic language translation that uses artificial neural networks. Unlike traditional statistical machine translation, NMT translates whole sentences at a time, considering the context of each word for a more accurate translation. It uses deep learning models to predict the likelihood of a sequence of words, typically modeling entire sentences in a single integrated model.
fields.label: Neural Machine Translation

fields.description: Neural Network Architecture Search (NAS) refers to the process of automatically finding the best neural network architecture for a specific task. In the context of Meta-Learning, it involves learning algorithms that can adapt quickly to new tasks. In NLP, it involves finding the optimal network structure for language processing tasks. The goal is to automate the design of machine learning models to reduce the need for manual tuning and to improve model performance.
fields.label: Neural Network Architecture Search

fields.description: Numerical Reasoning is a subfield of Reasoning that is concerned with understanding and processing numerical data. It involves performing arithmetic operations such as addition, subtraction, sorting, and counting.
fields.label: Numerical Reasoning

fields.description: Obfuscation refers to the process of altering text data in a way that it becomes less easily understood or interpreted by humans or machines, while still retaining the original meaning or information. This is often done for privacy protection, data anonymization, or to prevent automated systems from understanding sensitive information.
fields.label: Obfuscation

fields.description: Offensive Language Detection refers to the application of machine learning and AI techniques to identify and filter out offensive, inappropriate, or harmful language in text.
fields.label: Offensive Language Detection

fields.description: One-Hop Reasoning is a concept where the system uses a knowledge graph or text passage to answer simple queries by making a single "hop" or step from one entity to another. This involves identifying direct relationships or connections between entities in the graph or text passage. For example, if the query is about the capital of a country, the system would make one "hop" from the country to its capital in the knowledge graph or text passage.
fields.label: One-Hop Reasoning

fields.description: Ontologies encompass a representation, formal naming, and definition of categories, properties, and relations between concepts, data, and entities.
fields.label: Ontologies

fields.description: Ontology Learning focuses on the automatic or semi-automatic creation, evolution, and population of ontologies. It involves extracting information from various sources like text documents, databases, XML documents, etc., to create ontologies, which are structured sets of knowledge that include categories, properties, and relationships between entities.
fields.label: Ontology Learning

fields.description: Ontology Reasoning refers to the use of structured sets of knowledge (ontologies) to make inferences, draw conclusions, or make decisions. Ontologies, in this context, are a formal representation of knowledge within a domain, including the relationships between entities. This approach can help in understanding the context, semantics, and meaning of words in a text, thereby improving the accuracy of NLP tasks.
fields.label: Ontology Reasoning

fields.description: Open Book Question Answering is a type of natural language based QA (NLQA) where questions are expected to be answered with respect to a given set of open book facts, and common knowledge about a topic.
fields.label: Open Book Question Answering

fields.description: Open Domain Question Answering (ODQA) is a task in natural language processing that involves responding to questions about any topic without a specific domain limitation.
fields.label: Open Domain Question Answering

fields.description: Open Information Extraction is a subfield of Information Extraction & Text Mining that deals with the extraction of structured factual information from natural language text, usually in the form of triples or n-ary propositions, without relying on predefined schemas or templates.
fields.label: Open Information Extraction

fields.description: Opinion Mining is a subfield of Sentiment Analysis that deals with the automatic extraction and analysis of opinions, attitudes, and positions regarding a particular topic expressed in natural language texts.
fields.label: Opinion Mining

fields.description: Optical Character Recognition (OCR) is a technology that enables the conversion of printed or handwritten text and characters into machine-readable digital text. It is a process of digitizing text from physical documents, such as scanned paper documents, photographs, or images, and making the content accessible and editable on a computer or other digital devices.
fields.label: Optical Character Recognition

fields.description: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) is a method that aims to reduce the number of parameters that need to be fine-tuned in large pre-trained language models. This is achieved by freezing the majority of the parameters and only fine-tuning a small subset, which makes the process more efficient in terms of computational resources and time. This approach also helps to mitigate overfitting, especially when the available fine-tuning data is limited.
fields.label: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning

fields.description: Paraphrase Detection is the task of determining whether two text strings are paraphrases of each other. In other words, it involves identifying if the two given sentences convey the same meaning using different words or sentence structures.
fields.label: Paraphrase Detection

fields.description: Paraphrasing is a subfield of Text Generation that deals with the automatic generation of natural language text that expresses the same semantic meaning as a given input text, but using different words or syntactic structures. The goal of paraphrasing is to retain the original meaning while avoiding plagiarism, simplifying complex sentences, or adapting the language to a different audience.
fields.label: Paraphrasing

fields.description: A Parse Tree, or Syntax Tree, is a hierarchical representation of the syntactic structure of a sentence or text, showing how words and phrases are organized according to the grammar rules of a language. It visually illustrates how words are grouped into phrases and how those phrases relate to each other, helping to analyze the grammatical structure of the text.
fields.label: Parse Tree

fields.description: Part-of-Speech (PoS) Tagging is a process where grammatical tags or categories are assigned to each word (or token) in a sentence. These tags indicate the role of the word in the sentence, such as whether it's a noun, verb, adjective, adverb, etc.
fields.label: Part-of-Speech Tagging

fields.description: Passage Retrieval is a subfield of Information Retrieval that deals with retrieving relevant passages or snippets of text from a larger document or corpus in response to a user query. It involves developing algorithms and models that can identify and extract the most relevant and informative passages, and rank them based on their relevance and similarity to the query.
fields.label: Passage Retrieval

fields.description: Penn Discourse Treebank Discourse Parsing, often referred to as PDTB Discourse Parsing, is a natural language processing (NLP) task focused on analyzing and structuring the relationships and coherence between different parts of a text. It involves creating a tree-like structure that represents how sentences, phrases, or clauses in a text are connected in terms of discourse relations such as contrast, elaboration, and cause-effect. This parsing is typically done using the Penn Discourse Treebank dataset.
fields.label: Penn Discourse Treebank Discourse Parsing

fields.description: Phonetics is a subfield of Syntactic Text Processing that studies how humans produce and perceive sounds, or in the case of sign languages, the equivalent aspects of sign.
fields.label: Phonetics

fields.description: Phonology is a subfield of Syntactic Text Processing that studies the sound of languages or dialects and the patterns and rules that govern the use and combination of sounds to form meaningful units. It involves the analysis of phonemes, prosody, and intonation of speech, and the development of models and theories that can explain and predict the behavior and variability of sounds in different contexts.
fields.label: Phonology

fields.description: Phrase-based Machine Translation (PBMT) is a method that translates whole phrases instead of individual words to capture more context and meaning. This approach allows the system to handle differences in word order between languages and to translate common idioms or phrases that don't make sense when translated word by word. It uses statistical models to determine the most likely translation.
fields.label: Phrase-based Machine Translation

fields.description: Polarity Analysis is a subfield of Sentiment Analysis that deals with automatically detecting and classifying the polarity or valence of a given natural language text, such as positive, negative, or neutral.
fields.label: Polarity Analysis

fields.description: Political Bias is the tendency to favor a particular political party, ideology, or candidate, often resulting in presenting information in a way that unfairly supports one side over the other.
fields.label: Political Bias

fields.description: Positional Encoding is a technique used to give the model some information about the relative positions of the words in a sentence. It is used in transformer-based models where the order of words is not inherently considered. Positional encoding can be done in several ways, such as by adding a unique positional value to the word embeddings for each position in the sentence, or by using a sinusoidal function to generate positional encodings. This helps the model to understand the order of words and the grammar of the language.
fields.label: Positional Encoding

fields.description: Post-Training Quantization (PTQ) is a quantization technique where the model is quantized after it has been trained.
fields.label: Post-Training Quantization

fields.description: Pragmatics Modeling refers to the study and implementation of computational methods to understand and generate language that takes into account the context, speaker intentions, and the implied meaning beyond literal words and grammar. It focuses on how language is used in real-world situations and how context influences communication. Pragmatics modeling helps computers interpret and generate language that is contextually appropriate and conveys the intended meaning effectively.
fields.label: Pragmatic Modeling

fields.description: Privacy, Security & Safety in NLP refers to the protection of sensitive and usually personal information that may be contained within the data being processed. This includes ensuring that identifiable information is not disclosed during data analysis and that the data is stored and processed in a secure manner.
fields.label: Privacy, Security & Safety in NLP

fields.description: Proactive Learning is a generalization of active learning aimed at relaxing unrealistic assumptions and thereby reaching practical applications.
fields.label: Proactive Learning

fields.description: Probing refers to the process of investigating and understanding what kind of information a trained language model has learned. It involves creating tasks or tests that can reveal the model's knowledge about specific linguistic phenomena or its ability to perform certain tasks. The goal is to gain insights into the model's internal representations and understand its capabilities and limitations.
fields.label: Probing

fields.description: Profanity Obfuscation refers to the process of masking or altering offensive or inappropriate words in a text. This is often done to maintain the decency of content, prevent offensive language, and ensure that the content is suitable for all audiences. Techniques used may include replacing letters with symbols, removing the word entirely, or replacing it with a less offensive synonym.
fields.label: Profanity Obfuscation

fields.description: Programming Languages in NLP is a subfield of Multimodality that deals with the processing of programming languages and code in conjunction with natural language texts.
fields.label: Programming Languages in NLP

fields.description: Prompt Hacking describes a type of attack that exploits the vulnerabilities of large language models, by manipulating their inputs or prompts. Unlike traditional hacking, which typically exploits software vulnerabilities, prompt hacking relies on carefully crafting prompts to deceive the large language models into performing unintended actions.
fields.label: Prompt Hacking

fields.description: Prompt Injection refers to manipulating the language model’s output via engineered malicious prompts. This enables hackers to override original instructions and employed controls.
fields.label: Prompt Injection

fields.description: Prompt Injection Defense is the process of preventing prompt injection attacks.
fields.label: Prompt Injection Defense

fields.description: Prompt Optimization or Prompt Search refers to the process of fine-tuning the input or "prompt" given to a language model to improve its output. This can involve adjusting the phrasing, adding specific instructions, or using other techniques to guide the model towards generating more accurate, relevant, or creative responses. It's a way to control and enhance the performance of language models without modifying their internal parameters.
fields.label: Prompt Optimization

fields.description: Prompting refers to the process of providing a model with a specific input or "prompt" to guide its output or response. It's like asking a question or giving a command that the model responds to. Prompt Learning is a learning method where the model learns to generate appropriate responses to specific prompts. It's a way of training models to understand and respond to certain inputs in a desired manner. Prompt Engineering is the process of designing and optimizing prompts to get the best possible output from a model. It involves crafting effective prompts that can guide the model to produce more accurate, relevant, and useful responses.
fields.label: Prompting, Prompt Learning & Prompt Engineering

fields.description: Pronominal Anaphora Resolution refers to the process of determining the correct antecedent of a pronoun in a given text. Anaphora is a linguistic term that refers to the use of pronouns or other words to refer back to previously mentioned entities in a text. The resolution part involves correctly linking these pronouns to their intended referents, which is crucial for understanding the meaning of the text.
fields.label: Pronominal Anaphora Resolution

fields.description: Propaganda Detection aims at identifying and analyzing the use of persuasive or manipulative techniques in text, with the goal of recognizing content that aims to spread biased or misleading information, often for political or ideological purposes.
fields.label: Propaganda Detection

fields.description: Pseudonymization is the task of replacing personally identifiable information (PII) in such a way that it can be re-identified with the help of an identifier (additional information).
fields.label: Pseudonymization

fields.description: Psycholinguistics is a subfield of Linguistics & Cognitive NLP that studies the psychological and neural processes which enable humans to understand and use language.
fields.label: Psycholinguistics

fields.description: Quantization Aware Training means training the model from the start using quantized weights and activations. Quantization is done in the model training process rather than after the fact, which can result in higher accuracy than post-training quantization.
fields.label: Quantization Aware Training

fields.description: Query Expansion is used to improve the accuracy of information retrieval systems. It involves expanding the initial search query by adding synonyms, misspellings, alternative spellings, and related words to the original query. This helps in retrieving more relevant documents, even if they don't contain the exact original search terms.
fields.label: Query Expansion

fields.description: Query Representation refers to the process of transforming a user's information need into a suitable format or structure that can be processed by the retrieval system. The goal is to create a query that accurately represents the user's information need and can effectively retrieve relevant results from the database.
fields.label: Query Representation

fields.description: Question Answering is a subfield of Natural Language Interfaces that deals with the development of computer systems that can answer questions posed by humans in natural language. It involves the development of algorithms and models that can understand and interpret the meaning and intent of a question, retrieve relevant information from a knowledge base or document corpus, and generate a concise and accurate answer.
fields.label: Question Answering

fields.description: Question Classification (QC) refers to the task of categorizing questions into predefined classes. It is a crucial step in question answering systems where understanding the type of question can help in determining the kind of answer required. For example, a "who" question requires a person as an answer, while a "where" question requires a location.
fields.label: Question Classification

fields.description: Question Generation is a subfield of Text Generation that deals with the automatic generation of valid and fluent natural language questions based on given passages and target answers.
fields.label: Question Generation

fields.description: Race Bias, also known as Racial Bias, refers to the prejudiced attitudes, beliefs, or actions that an individual or institution holds towards a particular race or racial group.
fields.label: Race Bias

fields.description: Reasoning is a subfield of Natural Language Processing (NLP) that enables machines to draw logical conclusions and derive new knowledge from natural language texts based on the information available to them, using techniques such as deduction and induction.
fields.label: Reasoning

fields.description: A Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) is a type of artificial neural network designed to recognize patterns in sequences of data, such as text, genomes, handwriting, or spoken words. Unlike traditional neural networks, RNNs have loops, allowing information to persist, which makes them ideal for processing sequences. They are called recurrent because they perform the same task for every element of a sequence, with the output being dependent on the previous computations.
fields.label: Recurrent Neural Network

fields.description: Referring Expression Comprehension (REC) aims to localize a target object in an image described by a referring expression phrased in natural language.
fields.label: Referring Expression Comprehension

fields.description: Regularization is a technique used to prevent overfitting in deep learning models. This helps to ensure that the model generalizes well to unseen data, improving its overall performance and accuracy.
fields.label: Regularization

fields.description: Reinforcement Learning (RL) is a type of machine learning where an agent learns to make decisions by interacting with an environment. It receives feedback in the form of rewards or punishments based on its actions and uses this feedback to improve its decision-making over time.
fields.label: Reinforcement Learning

fields.description: Relation Directionality Classification refers to the task of determining the direction of a relationship or interaction between entities mentioned in text. It involves classifying whether one entity is the subject performing an action on another entity (e.g., "A is the parent of B") or vice versa (e.g., "B is the child of A"). This classification is essential for understanding the semantics and context of textual data.
fields.label: Relation Directionality Classification

fields.description: Relation Extraction is a subfield of Information Extraction & Text Mining that deals with identifying and extracting semantic relationships between entities mentioned in text. It involves identifying the relevant entities and the type of relationship that exists between them.
fields.label: Relation Extraction

fields.description: Relation Linking refers to the process of identifying the relations in a text and mapping them to the corresponding relations in a knowledge base.
fields.label: Relation Linking

fields.description: Representation Learning is a subfield of Semantic Text Processing that deals with the automatic learning and extraction of useful and compact representations of textual data, such as words, sentences, and documents, that can capture their semantic, syntactic, and pragmatic properties. It involves the development of algorithms and models that can transform natural language text into low-dimensional, dense, and informative vectors or embeddings that can be used in downstream tasks. This also includes learning vector representations of different modalities that can be used in NLP tasks.
fields.label: Representation Learning

fields.description: Responsible & Trustworthy NLP is a subfield of Natural Language Processing (NLP) that is concerned with implementing methods that focus on fairness, transparency, trustworthiness, explainability, accountability, and ethical aspects at its core. It involves considering the societal impact of NLP applications and ensuring that they do not perpetuate or amplify biases or discrimination. Additionally, responsible NLP also involves developing methods to ensure the privacy and security of user data, and to mitigate the risks of unintended consequences or misuse of NLP systems.
fields.label: Responsible & Trustworthy NLP

fields.description: Retrieval-based Dialogue Response Generation generates responses by selecting pre-existing responses from a predefined set of options or a database. It relies on retrieving the most appropriate response based on the input query or user message.
fields.label: Retrieval-based Dialogue Response Generation

fields.description: Retrieval-based Question Answering is a technique where a system selects the most appropriate answer from a predefined set of responses or a larger corpus of text based on the input question. It typically involves matching the question with candidate answers and selecting the one that best matches the query using various similarity or ranking methods.
fields.label: Retrieval-based Question Answering

fields.description: Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) is a concept that combines two key components: retrieval and generation. It involves retrieving relevant information from a large dataset or knowledge base and then using that information to generate natural language text or responses based on that retrieved information. RAG models typically consist of a retrieval module and a generation module, allowing them to access external knowledge to enhance the quality and relevance of generated text.
fields.label: Retrieval Augmented Generation

fields.description: Rhetorical Structure Theory (RST) is a framework used to analyze and represent the structure of texts by identifying the relationships between different parts of the text. It helps in understanding how different sentences or phrases within a text are interconnected to form a coherent and meaningful whole.
fields.label: Rhetorical Structure Theory

fields.description: Rhetorical Structure Theory (RST) Discourse Parsing aims to uncover the hierarchical and rhetorical structure of a text, such as how sentences and paragraphs are connected, through a well-defined tree structure.
fields.label: Rhetorical Structure Theory Discourse Parsing

fields.description: Rhetorical Structure Theory (RST) Discourse Tree refers to a representation of the hierarchical structure of a text's discourse or the way information is organized within a document. RST discourse trees break down a text into segments and show how these segments are related in terms of rhetorical relationships like "cause-effect," "contrast," "explanation," etc. These trees help analyze and understand the flow of information and coherence within a document.
fields.label: Rhetorical Structure Theory Discourse Tree

fields.description: Robustness NLP is a subfield of Responsible NLP that deals with developing algorithms and models that are insensitive to biases, resistant to data perturbations, and reliable for out-of-distribution predictions. Robust models can operate reliably and accurately even in the presence of biased, noisy or adversarial input, such as misspellings, grammatical errors, or intentional attacks.
fields.label: Robustness in NLP

fields.description: Rule-based dialogue response generation is a method of generating responses in a conversation by using predefined rules and patterns. Instead of relying on machine learning or natural language processing models, it follows explicit instructions or conditions to determine how to respond to user inputs. This approach is often used when precise and deterministic responses are required in dialogue systems and conversational agents.
fields.label: Rule-based Dialogue Response Generation

fields.description: Rule-based Machine Translation (RBMT) is a type of machine translation method that relies on sets of linguistic rules. These rules are used to transfer the syntactic structure of the source language into the target language. The rules are typically created by linguists and the system often includes a bilingual dictionary for word translation. RBMT can provide high accuracy for language pairs with similar grammatical structures, but it may struggle with languages that have very different syntax or grammar rules.
fields.label: Rule-based Machine Translation

fields.description: Rumor Detection refers to the task of identifying rumors from texts i.e. statements whose veracity is not quickly or ever confirmed, in utterances on social media platforms.
fields.label: Rumor Detection

fields.description: Sanitization is the task of removing sensitive or private information from a document so that it may be distributed to a broader audience. In a naive way, this simply involves blackening out sensitive parts in texts.
fields.label: Sanitization

fields.description: Sarcasm Detection refers to the ability of AI systems to identify and understand sarcasm in text. It's a challenging aspect of sentiment analysis, as sarcasm often involves expressing negative sentiments using positive words in a context, making it difficult for machines to interpret. This requires advanced NLP techniques, including understanding of context, tone, and often cultural or situational nuances.
fields.label: Sarcasm Detection

fields.description: Scene Text Recognition is a task that involves automatically identifying and localizing text within natural images or videos. The goal of scene text detection is to develop algorithms that can robustly detect and and label text with bounding boxes in uncontrolled and complex environments, such as street signs, billboards, or license plates.
fields.label: Scene Text Recognition

fields.description: Segmented Discourse Representation Theory (SDRT) Discourse Parsing is an approach that focuses on structuring and understanding written or spoken language at a discourse level. It involves breaking down a text or conversation into segments or clauses, assigning semantic representations to these segments, and analyzing the relationships between them to capture the discourse's overall meaning and coherence.
fields.label: Segmented Discourse Representation Theory Discopurse Parsing

fields.description: Self-supervised Learning is a type of machine learning where the model learns to predict a part of the input data from other parts of the same input data. It does not require explicit labels provided by humans. Instead, it uses the structure of the data itself to generate labels. For example, in NLP, a model might be trained to predict the next word in a sentence, using the previous words as input, thereby learning the syntax, semantics, and other language rules.
fields.label: Self-supervised Learning

fields.description: Semantic Matching refers to the process of identifying and linking words, phrases, or sentences that share similar meanings, even if they do not share the same surface form or structure. This involves understanding the context, synonyms, and intent behind the words, rather than just matching the exact words or phrases.
fields.label: Semantic Matching

fields.description: Semantic Parsing is a subfield of Semantic Text Processing that deals with the problem of mapping the meaning of natural language expressions into formal representations, such as logical forms, knowledge graphs, or database queries. It involves developing algorithms and models that can parse and understand the syntax, semantics, and pragmatics of a sentence and generate a structured representation of its meaning.
fields.label: Semantic Parsing

fields.description: Semantic Search & Search Engines is a subfield of Semantic Text Processing and Information Retrieval that deals with the retrieval and ranking of information and documents based on their meaning and relevance to a user's query. It involves developing algorithms and models that can understand and analyze the semantic and pragmatic aspects of a query and a document, such as context, ambiguity, and intent, and generate a ranked list of relevant and diverse results.
fields.label: Semantic Search & Search Engines

fields.description: Semantic Similarity is a subfield of Semantic Text Processing that deals with the quantification and comparison of the semantic similarity or relatedness between two or more pieces of text, such as words, sentences, phrases, or documents. It includes metrics that estimate the distance or semantic relatedness of texts based on their meanings.
fields.label: Semantic Similarity

fields.description: Semantic Text Processing is a subfield of Natural Language Processing (NLP) that attempts to derive meaning from natural language and helps machines interpret textual data semantically. It involves developing algorithms and models that can understand and represent the semantics of words and sentences, and the relationships between them.
fields.label: Semantic Text Processing

fields.description: A Semantic Treebank is a structured dataset or corpus that annotates sentences or text with detailed semantic information, often represented as labeled tree structures. These tree structures capture the relationships and meanings of words and phrases within the text.
fields.label: Semantic Treebank

fields.description: Semi-supervised learning is a machine learning approach where the model is trained using a combination of a small amount of labeled data and a large amount of unlabeled data. The idea is to use the unlabeled data to enhance the learning accuracy of the model derived from the labeled data. This method is particularly useful when it's expensive or time-consuming to label data but unlabeled data is abundant.
fields.label: Semi-supervised Learning

fields.description: Sentence Transformers is a framework that provides an easy method to compute dense vector representations for sentences and paragraphs. These representations (also known as embeddings) can then be compared for semantic similarity. This is achieved by fine-tuning transformer networks, like BERT, on specific NLP tasks, such as natural language inference.
fields.label: Sentence-Transformers

fields.description: Sentence Alignment refers to the process of identifying corresponding sentences in two different languages within a parallel corpus. This is a crucial step in training statistical machine translation models as it helps the model to learn how words and phrases in one language translate into another. The alignment is usually done based on sentence length and order, but more complex methods may also consider the actual content of the sentences.
fields.label: Sentence Alignment

fields.description: Sentence Embeddings refer to the numerical representation of sentences or short paragraphs in a multi-dimensional vector space. It is a form of feature extraction where sentences or short paragraphs are converted into vectors. These vectors capture the semantic meaning of the sentence, allowing similar sentences to be mapped close to each other in the vector space.
fields.label: Sentence Embeddings

fields.description: Sentiment Analysis is a subfield of Natural Language Processing (NLP) that deals with the identification, extraction and quantification of affective states and subjective information from textual data.
fields.label: Sentiment Analysis

fields.description: Sequence Labeling is a task where the model is trained to assign a label to each member in the sequence of input data. This is commonly used in NLP tasks such as part-of-speech tagging, named entity recognition, and text chunking where each word in a sentence needs to be labeled based on its role.
fields.label: Sequence Labeling

fields.description: Sign Language Recognition is a computer vision and natural language processing task that involves automatically recognizing and translating sign language gestures into written or spoken language. The goal of sign language recognition is to develop algorithms that can understand and interpret sign language, enabling people who use sign language as their primary mode of communication to communicate more easily with non-signers.
fields.label: Sign Language Recognition

fields.description: Slang Detection and Identification refers to the process of identifying and understanding slang words or phrases in a given text. Slang words are informal language, often specific to certain groups or cultures, and can be challenging for NLP algorithms to interpret due to their non-standard usage.
fields.label: Slang Detection

fields.description: Slot filling is a concept used in various applications, particularly in chatbots, virtual assistants, and information extraction systems. It involves identifying and extracting specific pieces of information, known as "slots," from unstructured text or user input. These slots typically correspond to specific categories or entities, such as dates, names, locations, or any other predefined information. For instance, when a user queries for nearby restaurants, key slots for location and preferred food are required for a dialog system to retrieve the appropriate information. Thus, the main challenge in the slot-filling task is to extract the target entity.
fields.label: Slot Filling

fields.description: Social Bias refers to discrimination for, or against, a person or group, or a set of ideas or beliefs, in a way that is prejudicial or unfair. Social bias often involves consciously or unconsciously stereotyping others and behaving in a way that disadvantages a person or group or advantages another. Social bias, both implicit and explicit, is at the core of racism, misogyny and discrimination based on sexual orientation or religion, and such biases may operate between individuals or at the level of the institution.
fields.label: Social Bias

fields.description: Soft Prompts are learnable, continuous feature vectors that are added to the input prompt. Unlike hard prompts, they are learned during the training process and aren’t human-readable.
fields.label: Soft Prompts

fields.description: Span Detection refers to the task of identifying and categorizing specific portions or spans of text within a larger document or corpus. These spans can be words, phrases, or even whole sentences that are relevant to the task at hand.
fields.label: Span Detection

fields.description: Sparse Document Retrieval refers to the process of finding the most relevant documents in a large dataset based on a specific query. This is typically done by creating a sparse representation of the documents, where each document is represented as a high-dimensional vector with most values being zero. The non-zero values in the vector represent the presence of specific words or phrases in the document. The relevance of a document to a query is then determined by comparing these vectors.
fields.label: Sparse Document Retrieval

fields.description: Sparse Embeddings refer to the representation of words or phrases in a high-dimensional space where most of the elements are zero. This is in contrast to dense embeddings where all elements carry some value. Sparse embeddings can be beneficial in situations where the dataset is large and complex, as they can reduce computational load and memory requirements. However, they may not capture semantic relationships between words as effectively as dense embeddings.
fields.label: Sparse Embeddings

fields.description: Sparse Passage Retrieval in refers to the method of extracting relevant sections or passages from a large text corpus based on keyword matching. It uses traditional information retrieval techniques, such as Bag of Words or TF-IDF, to identify and retrieve passages that are most likely to contain the answer to a given query. This approach is called "sparse" because it does not consider the semantic relationships between words and often results in a high-dimensional, sparse vector representation of the text.
fields.label: Sparse Passage Retrieval

fields.description: Speaker diarization is a process that involves identifying and distinguishing different speakers in an audio recording or a continuous stream of speech. The primary goal of speaker diarization is to segment the audio into distinct speaker segments and associate each segment with a specific speaker identity.
fields.label: Speaker Diarization

fields.description: Speaker Recognition refers to the technique of identifying a person based on their voice characteristics.
fields.label: Speaker Recognition

fields.description: Speaker Verification is a process used to confirm the claimed identity of a speaker based on their voice characteristics. It involves comparing the speaker's voice with a previously stored voice model or voiceprint.
fields.label: Speaker Verification

fields.description: Speech and Audo-specific Language Models refers to specialized language models that are designed and trained to understand and generate human language specifically in the context of speech and audio data. These models are tailored to handle spoken language and sound-related tasks.
fields.label: Speech & Audio-specific Language Models

fields.description: Speech & Audio in NLP is a subfield of Multimodality that deals with the processing of spoken language and audio data in conjunction with textual data. It involves developing algorithms and models that can recognize and transcribe speech and audio, understand and interpret their meaning, and generate natural language responses.
fields.label: Speech & Audio in NLP

fields.description: Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR), or Speech-to-Text (STT), is a technology that converts spoken language into written text. It is a field that focuses on the development of systems and algorithms capable of transcribing spoken language accurately. ASR systems are designed to understand and interpret human speech, allowing computers to process and analyze spoken words.
fields.label: Automatic Speech Recognition

fields.description: Speech segmentation refers to the process of dividing continuous spoken language or audio signals into smaller, meaningful units or segments such as words, syllables, or phonemes. These segments are typically characterized by pauses, changes in prosody (intonation and rhythm), or other acoustic features that signal the boundaries between different linguistic units. The primary goal of speech segmentation is to break down a continuous stream of speech into discrete, manageable units for further analysis or processing.
fields.label: Speech Segmentation

fields.description: Speech synthesis, also known as text-to-speech (TTS), is a technology that converts text or written content into spoken language. It is a process through which a computer or electronic device generates human-like speech by translating textual input into audible speech output.
fields.label: Speech Synthesis

fields.description: Spell Checking refers to the process of identifying and correcting spelling mistakes in text. It involves comparing each word in a text to a dictionary of correctly spelled words, and suggesting corrections for misspelled words.
fields.label: Spell Checking

fields.description: Spoken Language Understanding (SLU) focuses on the development of technologies and systems capable of processing and comprehending spoken language. The primary goal of SLU is to enable machines, such as voice assistants or automated customer service systems, to understand and extract meaning from spoken language input provided by humans.
fields.label: Spoken Language Understanding

fields.description: Stance Detection refers to the task of determining the attitude or stance of a speaker or writer with respect to some topic or the overall contextual polarity of a document. The stance could be in favor, against, or neutral towards the target topic.
fields.label: Stance Detection

fields.description: Static Embeddings refer to the method of representing words in a fixed, pre-trained vector space. Each word is assigned a specific vector that does not change regardless of the context in which the word is used. This method, while computationally efficient, does not account for the dynamic nature of language where the meaning of a word can change based on its surrounding context.
fields.label: Static Embeddings

fields.description: Statistical Machine Translation (SMT) is a method of machine translation where the translation of text is generated on the basis of statistical models. These models are derived from the analysis of bilingual text corpora. The system learns to translate by being trained on large amounts of existing translations. It uses probability distributions to select the most likely translation among multiple possibilities.
fields.label: Statistical Machine Translation

fields.description: Stemming refers to the process of reducing inflected (or sometimes derived) words to their word stem or root form. The main purpose of stemming is to bring variation forms of a word back to its base form, such as "running" to "run".
fields.label: Stemming

fields.description: Story Generation is the task of automatically generating a coherent narrative, often from a set of premises or a brief summary.
fields.label: Story Generation

fields.description: Structured Data-specific Language Models are trained to understand and generate text related to structured data formats, such as tables, graphs, databases, JSON, XML, or other organized data structures.
fields.label: Structured Data-specific Language Models

fields.description: Structured Data in NLP is a subfield of Multimodality that deals with the processing of structured data such as tables or graphs in conjunction with textual data. It involves the development of algorithms and models that can extract, represent, and use structured data in natural language form.
fields.label: Structured Data in NLP

fields.description: Stylistic Analysis is a subfield of Sentiment Analysis that deals with automatically analyzing the stylistic features and patterns in a given text, such as tone, mood, and writing style to extract the meaning or message contained in texts.
fields.label: Stylistic Analysis

fields.description: Subjectivity Classification refers to the process of determining whether a given text or sentence is subjective (expressing personal opinions, beliefs, emotions, judgments) or objective (providing factual information).
fields.label: Subjectivity Classification

fields.description: Text Summarization is a subfield of Information Extraction & Text Mining and Text Generation that deals with the automatic generation of a concise and coherent summary of a longer text. It involves developing algorithms and models that can identify the most important information in a text and generate a summary that captures the essence of the original text.
fields.label: Summarization

fields.description: Syntactic Parsing is a subfield of Syntactic Text Processing that deals with automatically analyzing the syntactic structure of a sentence or text, and representing it in a formal or graphical form, such as a parse tree or dependency graph. It involves developing algorithms and models that can identify and classify the syntactic constituents, such as noun phrases and verb phrases, and their relationships in a sentence, and generate a structured representation of the sentence.
fields.label: Syntactic Parsing

fields.description: Syntactic Path refers to the grammatical relationships between words in a sentence. These paths are used to understand the structure of a sentence and the dependencies between words. They are often represented in a tree-like structure, known as a parse tree, where each node represents a word and the edges represent the syntactic relationships between words.
fields.label: Syntactic Paths

fields.description: Syntactic Text Processing is a subfield of Natural Language Processing (NLP) that deals with the analysis of the syntax and grammatical structure of natural language texts.
fields.label: Syntactic Text Processing

fields.description: A "Syntactic Treebank" is a collection of sentences from a text corpus, where each sentence is parsed and represented as a syntactic tree. These trees break down the sentence's structure, showing how words and phrases relate to each other grammatically.
fields.label: Syntactic Treebank

fields.description: Syntax-based Machine Translation is a type of machine translation approach that uses syntactic information from the source language to generate more accurate translations in the target language. It involves parsing the source language into a syntactic tree or structure, then transforming this into a similar structure in the target language, and finally generating the target language text from this structure. This approach can better handle differences in word order and grammatical structures between languages compared to phrase-based or word-based machine translation methods.
fields.label: Syntax-based Machine Translation

fields.description: Table-to-Text Generation is the task of generating natural language descriptions from tabular data.
fields.label: Table-to-Text

fields.description: Table Question Answering (Table QA) is a task that involves extracting answers from structured tabular data using natural language questions. It focuses on understanding and querying information stored in tables, such as databases or spreadsheets, to provide relevant responses to user queries.
fields.label: Table Question Answering

fields.description: Tagging is a subfield of Syntactic Text Processing that deals with automatically assigning labels or tags to words or other units in a natural language texts, based on their grammatical or syntactic properties.
fields.label: Tagging

fields.description: Taxonomies are systems for classifying and organizing things or concepts, typically arranged in a hierarchical structure.
fields.label: Taxonomies

fields.description: Taxonomy Learning refers to the process of automatically generating a hierarchical classification of concepts, entities or terms from a large amount of text data. It involves identifying relationships between different terms and organizing them into a tree-like structure, where each node represents a concept or category and each edge represents a relationship between two concepts.
fields.label: Taxonomy Learning

fields.description: Term Extraction is a subfield of Information Extraction & Text Mining that deals with identifying and extracting relevant terms such as keywords or keyphrases from natural language texts.
fields.label: Term Extraction

fields.description: Text-to-Image refers to the process of generating visual content, such as images or illustrations, based on textual descriptions or input.
fields.label: Text-to-Image

fields.description: Text-to-Image Retrieval refers to the process of finding and retrieving relevant images based on a given text query. It involves using natural language processing techniques to understand textual descriptions and then searching for images that best match or represent the content described in the text.
fields.label: Text-to-Image Retrieval

fields.description: Text-to-SQL is a task where the goal is to automatically generate SQL queries from natural language text. The task involves converting the text input into a semantically correct SQL query that can be executed on a database.
fields.label: Text-to-SQL

fields.description: Text-to-Structured Data refers to the process of converting unstructured or semi-structured textual information into a structured format that can be more easily analyzed, processed, and stored by computers. This conversion involves extracting meaningful data and organizing it into a structured representation, typically in the form of a database, spreadsheet, or some other structured data format.
fields.label: Text-to-Structured Data

fields.description: Text-to-Video is a process that involves generating video content from textual input or descriptions.
fields.label: Text-to-Video

fields.description: Text Classification is a subfield of Information Retrieval and Information Extraction & Text Mining that deals with automatically assigning a label or class to a natural language text. It involves the development of algorithms and models that can learn to recognize patterns in texts and classify them into predefined categories.
fields.label: Text Classification

fields.description: Text Clustering is a subfield of Information Extraction & Text Mining that deals with grouping similar documents or sentences into clusters based on their content. The goal of text clustering is to discover patterns in large amounts of unstructured text data and identify groups of documents that share common themes, topics, or features.
fields.label: Text Clustering

fields.description: Text Complexity is a subfield of Semantic Text Processing that deals with the analysis and assessment of the difficulty, readability, and suitability of texts for different audiences and purposes. It can be assessed based on a series of factors, such as the readability of the text, the levels of meaning or purpose in the text, the structure of the text, the conventionality and clarity of the language, and the knowledge demands of the text.
fields.label: Text Complexity

fields.description: Text Embeddings refer to the representation of text in the form of vectors. The underlying idea is to convert text into a numerical form that can be easily processed by machines. These embeddings capture the semantic meaning or context of words or sentences, where similar words or sentences are closer in the vector space.
fields.label: Text Embeddings

fields.description: Text Error Correction is a subfield of Syntactic Text Processing that deals with automatically detecting and correcting grammatical errors in a text, such as spelling mistakes, word choice errors, or syntax errors. It involves developing algorithms and models that can identify and diagnose the errors, generate corrected versions of the text, and evaluate the quality and accuracy of the corrections.
fields.label: Text Error Correction

fields.description: Text Generation is a subfield of Natural Language Processing (NLP) which attempts to teach machines to automatically generate texts that are indistinguishable from texts written by humans.
fields.label: Text Generation

fields.description: Text Normalization is a subfield of Syntactic Text Processing that deals with the process of transforming text into a single canonical form that it might not have had before. It reduces variations in word forms to a common form when the variations mean the same thing by converting word tokens to their base form.
fields.label: Text Normalization

fields.description: Text Regression refers to the application of regression analysis on text data. It involves predicting a continuous value (like a rating or a price) based on text data.
fields.label: Text Regression

fields.description: Text Representations aim to capture the semantic meaning, context, or sentiment of texts so they can be understood and processed by machines.
fields.label: Text Representations

fields.description: Text Scrubbing transforms or maps data into a format that can be easily analyzed. This may include removing punctuation, numbers, special characters, converting all text to lower or upper case, removing stop words, stemming, lemmatization, etc.
fields.label: Text Scrubbing

fields.description: Text Segmentation is a subfield of Syntactic Text Processing that deals with automatically dividing a text into smaller segments or units that can be analyzed or processed separately. It involves developing algorithms and models that can identify and classify the structural or semantic boundaries between different sections or paragraphs in a text, and group them into meaningful and coherent segments.
fields.label: Text Segmentation

fields.description: Text Simplification (TS) is the process of transforming complex text into a simpler version that retains the original meaning. It involves reducing the linguistic complexity of the text, making it easier to read and understand. This can include simplifying vocabulary, grammar, or sentence structure. It's particularly useful for aiding language learning, improving readability for people with cognitive disabilities, or for processing text in machine learning algorithms.
fields.label: Text Simplification

fields.description: Text Style Transfer is a subfield of Text Generation that deals with adapting and/or changing the stylistic manner in which a text is written, while preserving the semantic meaning of the original text.
fields.label: Text Style Transfer

fields.description: Textual Inference is a subfield of Reasoning that deals with the task of automatically determining whether a natural-language hypothesis can be inferred from a given premise, predicting their logical relationship, such as entailment, contradiction, or neutral.
fields.label: Textual Inference

fields.description: Thesaurus is a tool that lists words grouped together according to similarity of meaning. It is used for identifying synonyms, antonyms, and related terms to enhance the understanding and processing of language data.
fields.label: Thesaurus

fields.description: Tokenization is the process of breaking down a large paragraph of text into smaller parts, known as tokens. These tokens can be morphemes, word pieces, words, phrases, or sentences.
fields.label: Tokenization

fields.description: Topic Classification is a machine learning technique used to categorize text or spoken language into predefined topics or categories. It involves training a model on a set of labeled texts, each associated with one or more topics. Once trained, the model can then be used to predict the topics of new, unseen texts.
fields.label: Topic Classification

fields.description: Topic Modeling is a subfield of Information Extraction & Text Mining that deals with automatically discovering latent topics or themes in a large corpus of natural language text. It involves developing algorithms and models that can identify and extract the main themes or topics in the text, and cluster the documents based on their topic distribution.
fields.label: Topic Modeling

fields.description: Transformers & Large Language Models is concerned with models based on the transformer neural network architecture that introduced the attention mechanism and has become foundational in various machine learning applications. In addition, this concept includes Large Language Models, a specific application of transformers that are pre-trained on large amounts of textual data and excel at various natural language processing tasks.
fields.label: Transformers & Large Language Models

fields.description: Translation Memory (TM) is a database that stores sentences, paragraphs, or segments of text that have been previously translated, to aid in the translation of new texts. It allows for the reuse of translations, improving translation efficiency and consistency.
fields.label: Translation Memory

fields.description: Tree typically refers to a hierarchical data structure.
fields.label: Tree

fields.description: Tree Fragments refer to smaller parts or substructures of a parse tree. A parse tree represents the syntactic structure of a sentence according to a particular grammar.
fields.label: Tree Fragments

fields.description: A Treebank is a corpus or collection of text samples that have been manually annotated usually with syntactic or grammatical structure in the form of parse trees. These parse trees represent the hierarchical structure of sentences, showing how words are related and organized in phrases and clauses. In addition to syntactic treebanks, semantic treebanks combine syntactical trees of sentences with the formal representation of their meaning in logical form.
fields.label: Treebank

fields.description: Triple Classification is a task of determining whether a given triple (subject, predicate, object) is correct or not based on the existing knowledge in the graph. It is a binary classification problem where the goal is to predict if a triple is true (exists in the graph) or false (does not exist in the graph).
fields.label: Triple Classification

fields.description: Typology is a subfield of Syntactic Text Processing and Multilinguality that deals with studying the diversity and commonalities of the grammatical structures and patterns in different languages to allow their comparison. Its aim is to describe and explain the structural diversity and the common properties of the world's languages.
fields.label: Typology

fields.description: Unsupervised Learning refers to the machine learning task where a model learns and identifies patterns directly from unlabelled text data. This method does not require a predefined set of labels or training data.
fields.label: Unsupervised Learning

fields.description: Verdict Prediction attempts to determine the veracity of a claim. The simplest approach is binary classification, for example, labeling a claim as true or false.
fields.label: Verdict Prediction

fields.description: Video-Text Retrieval (VTR) aims to search for the most relevant video related to the semantics in a given sentence, and vice versa.
fields.label: Video-Text Retrieval

fields.description: Video captioning is the process of adding textual descriptions or subtitles to a video, typically in real-time or as a post-production step. The primary purpose of video captioning is to make video content accessible to a wider audience, including those who are deaf or hard of hearing, as well as non-native speakers and individuals in noisy environments where audio may be difficult to hear.
fields.label: Video Captioning

fields.description: Video Question Answering (VideoQA) aims to answer natural language questions related to the content of a given video.
fields.label: Video Question Answering

fields.description: Vision-specific Language Models refers to specialized language models that are designed and trained to understand and generate human language specifically in the context of visual data such as images and video.
fields.label: Vision-specific Language Models

fields.description: Visual Commonsense Reasoning is cognition-level visual understanding task. Given a challenging question about an image, machines need to present two sub-tasks: answer correctly and provide a rationale justifying its answer.
fields.label: Visual Commonsense Reasoning

fields.description: Visual Data in NLP is a subfield of Multimodality that deals with the processing of visual data such as images or videos in conjunction with textual data.
fields.label: Visual Data in NLP

fields.description: Visual Entailment (VE) is the task of determining whether a visual premise implies a textual hypothesis. The prediction can be either an entailment, neutral or a contradiction.
fields.label: Visual Entailment

fields.description: Visual Question Answering (VQA) is the task of answering open-ended questions based on visual input such as images or videos. The output consists of natural language responses to natural language questions.
fields.label: Visual Question Answering

fields.description: Visual reasoning is a task that requires multimodal perception and commonsense cognition of the world. It demands models to not only comprehend and interpret visual information but also to apply high-level cognition to derive logical conclusions.
fields.label: Visual Reasoning

fields.description: Weak Supervision refers to the process of using less precise, often noisier sources of supervision to train machine learning models. This approach is typically used when there is a lack of sufficient labeled data for training. Weak supervision may involve heuristics or rules to generate labels.
fields.label: Weak Supervision

fields.description: Word-based Machine Translation is a method where the translation from the source language to the target language is performed on a word-by-word basis. It involves direct substitution of words in one language for words in another. However, this approach often fails to capture the context and grammatical differences between languages, leading to inaccurate or nonsensical translations.
fields.label: Word-based Machine Translation

fields.description: Word Alignment refers to the process of identifying which word or group of words in the source language corresponds to which word or group of words in the target language. This alignment is crucial for accurate translation as it helps in understanding the relationship between the words in different languages, thereby improving the quality of the translation.
fields.label: Word Alignment

fields.description: Word Embeddings refer to words or phrases that are mapped to vectors of real numbers. These vectors capture the semantic and syntactic meaning, relationship with other words, and context of the words in a compact way.
fields.label: Word Embeddings

fields.description: Word Sense Disambiguation is a subfield of Semantic Text Processing that deals with the problem of identifying the correct meaning or sense of a word in a given context, which can be ambiguous or polysemous. It involves developing algorithms and models that can analyze the syntactic and semantic features of a sentence and disambiguate the senses of the words in it, based on their co-occurrence patterns, collocations, and relations with other words.
fields.label: Word Sense Disambiguation

fields.description: Word Sense Induction (WSI) is widely known as the “unsupervised version” of WSD. The problem states as: Given a target word (e.g., “cold”) and a collection of sentences (e.g., “I caught a cold”, “The weather is cold”) that use the word, cluster the sentences according to their different senses/meanings. We do not need to know the sense/meaning of each cluster, but sentences inside a cluster should have used the target words with the same sense.
fields.label: Word Sense Induction

fields.description: Zero-shot Entailment is a method where a model, without being explicitly trained on any classification task, can classify unseen text into one or more categories. This is achieved by leveraging Natural Language Inference (NLI) models. The model is presented with a text and a hypothesis (usually a statement about the category), and it predicts whether the hypothesis can be inferred from the text. This allows the model to classify text into categories it has never seen during training, hence the term "zero-shot".
fields.label: Zero-shot Entailment

fields.description: Zero-shot Learning refers to the ability of a model to understand and perform tasks it has not been explicitly trained on. It involves training a model on a set of tasks or languages, and then the model uses that knowledge to understand and perform new tasks or understand new languages. This concept is particularly useful in situations where labeled data is scarce or unavailable.
fields.label: Zero-shot Learning

fields.description: Zero Anaphora (ZA) Resolution refers to the process of identifying and resolving implicit or unstated subjects or objects in a sentence. It's a type of anaphora where the anaphoric expression is not overtly present in the discourse. This is common in many languages where the subject or object of a sentence can be dropped if it can be inferred from the context. The challenge in NLP is to correctly infer these missing elements to understand the complete meaning of the sentence.
fields.label: Zero Anaphora Resolution

fields.description: An n-gram is a contiguous sequence of n items from a given sample of text or speech. N can be any integer number, and the items can be phonemes, syllables, letters, words or base pairs according to the application. For example, in a sentence, a 1-gram (or unigram) would be each individual word, a 2-gram (or bigram) would be each sequence of two words, a 3-gram (or trigram) would be each sequence of three words, and so on.
fields.label: n-gram

fields.description: n-gram Language Models are a probabilistic language models used to predict the next word in a sentence based on the previous 'n' words. It uses the statistical properties of n-grams to predict the sequence of words in a sentence. The 'n' in n-gram represents the number of words considered as context. For example, in a bigram model (n=2), the next word is predicted based on the previous word, while in a trigram model (n=3), the next word is predicted based on the previous two words.
fields.label: n-gram Language Model
